spot_story_tteunbongsaem.title: Tteunbongsaem Spring, Source of the Geumgang River
spot_story_tteunbongsaem.subtitle: 10-18 Mulppuraengi-gil, Jangsu-gun (Geumgang Love Water Experience Center)
spot_story_tteunbongsaem.pull_quote: Where King Taejo Yi Seong-gye witnessed a mythical phoenix soaring on a five-colored rainbow and received the omen to found the Joseon Dynasty — the very headwaters of the Geumgang River flowing 397.25 km to the West Sea.
paragraphs: Ascending 1.5 km along the valley of Sinmusan Mountain in Subun Village brings you to Tteunbongsaem Spring, the ultimate source of the Geumgang River. Legend tells that King Taejo Yi Seong-gye, founder of the Joseon Dynasty, offered prayers here and received a divine revelation to establish the new dynasty after seeing a phoenix rise into the sky atop a rainbow.

From this quiet spring, the stream journeys 397.25 km all the way to the West Sea estuary. The surrounding Tteunbongsaem Ecological Park features the Geumgang Love Water Experience Center, native wildflower colonies, an eco-playground, an ecological greenhouse, and forest trails. Showcasing endangered species, amphibians, and reptiles, it offers visitors enriching ecological education and memorable outdoor experiences.

spot_story_deogyusan.subtitle: 530-62 Gucheondong-ro, Mupung-myeon, Muju-gun
spot_story_deogyusan.pull_quote: Beneath soaring, majestic Norway spruces reaching toward the sky, immerse yourself in the serene, deep breath of the forest across all four seasons.
paragraphs: Nestled beside Deogyusan National Park and Gucheondong Valley, Deogyusan Natural Recreation Forest offers deep woodland relaxation throughout the year: vibrant royal azaleas in spring, crystal-clear streams in summer, fiery autumn foliage on Jeoksangsan Mountain, and breathtaking rime frost with snowy vistas in winter.

The recreation forest is densely populated with Japanese larches and Korean pines, alongside its signature highlight: a magnificent Norway spruce forest planted in 1931. Soaring gracefully toward the heavens with an exotic, grand ambiance, the gentle woodland trails allow anyone to enjoy a rejuvenating phytoncide walk.

spot_story_baengnyeonsa.title: Gangjin Mandeoksan Baengnyeonsa Camellia Forest & Dasan Trail
spot_story_baengnyeonsa.subtitle: 145 Baengnyeonsa-gil, Doam-myeon, Gangjin-gun (Natural Monument No. 151)
spot_story_baengnyeonsa.pull_quote: An 800-meter woodland trail where Dasan Jeong Yak-yong and Master Hyejang strolled to share tea and philosophy, embraced by 1,500 native camellia trees.
paragraphs: Surrounding the historic Baengnyeonsa Temple—where Venerable Wonmyo organized the White Lotus Society during the Goryeo Dynasty—thrives a lush forest of around 1,500 indigenous camellia trees designated as Natural Monument No. 151. Beginning to bud as crisp winds arrive in late autumn and early winter, they carpet the tranquil path with crimson blossoms well into early spring.

Passing through a 7-meter-high camellia canopy toward Dasan Chodang thatched house, this serene hillside path is where renowned scholar Dasan Jeong Yak-yong walked daily during his exile to meet Master Hyejang. Along this path of contemplation, visitors are treated to panoramic views overlooking the placid waters of Gangjin Bay.

spot_story_cheongnyeongpo.title: Yeongwol Cheongnyeongpo Cape, King Danjong's Forest Surrounded by Water
spot_story_cheongnyeongpo.subtitle: Gwangcheon-ri, Nam-myeon, Yeongwol-gun, Gangwon (Scenic Site No. 50)
spot_story_cheongnyeongpo.pull_quote: A secluded inland island accessible only by boat; ancient pine groves and the majestic Gwaneumsong tree quietly witnessing a young king's tragic exile.
paragraphs: Located along the winding Seogang River in the upper reaches of the Namhangang River, Cheongnyeongpo Cape is surrounded by deep water on three sides and flanked by the sheer cliffs of Yukyukbong Peak to the west. Accessible solely by ferry, this naturally secluded sanctuary is where King Danjong, the 6th monarch of the Joseon Dynasty, was exiled after his dethronement.

Stepping off the short ferry ride, visitors are welcomed by a dense pine grove carrying centuries of history and the venerable Gwaneumsong Pine Tree (Natural Monument No. 349). Ascending to Manghyangtap Pagoda and Nosandae Cliff, the tranquil currents of the Seogang River blend with autumn leaves and pine fragrance, leaving a deeply resonant impression.

spot_story_suncheonman.subtitle: 513-25 Suncheonman-gil, Suncheon-si (UNESCO World Natural Heritage)
spot_story_suncheonman.pull_quote: Korea's premier ecological garden where hooded cranes soar over endless golden reed waves and the S-shaped tidal channel glows in evening crimson.
paragraphs: Gently cradled by the Goheung and Yeosu peninsulas, Suncheonman Bay is an expansive coastal wetland spanning over 75 km². From autumn through winter, vast colonies of tall golden reeds sway like shimmering silver waves, creating a magnificent spectacle.

Strolling along the barrier-free wooden boardwalks accessible to strollers and wheelchairs, visitors can observe thriving mudflats brimming with crabs and mudskippers. An easy climb up to Yongsan Observatory unveils an unforgettable sunset descending across the iconic S-shaped waterway.

spot_story_jusanji.subtitle: Jusanji-ri, Juwangsan-myeon, Cheongsong-gun, Gyeongbuk (Scenic Site No. 105)
spot_story_jusanji.pull_quote: A mystical mountain reservoir built in 1721 that has never dried up, weaving a watercolor morning of submerged King Willows and ethereal water mist.
paragraphs: Completed in 1721 during the reign of Joseon King Gyeongjong, Jusanji Reservoir rests atop dense welded tuff formations formed from volcanic ash. For over 300 years, this enchanting mountain pond has never run dry or exposed its bottom, even through the severest droughts.

In the early morning when delicate mist drifts low across the water, over twenty centuries-old King Willows rooted deep in the lake cast serene reflections upon the mirror-like surface, quietly drawing photographers and travelers year-round.

story_seoul_visitseoul_guide.source_book: Seoul Tourism Organization Visit Seoul 《2026 Seoul Tourism Guidebook》 Web Edition
story_seoul_visitseoul_guide.title: 《2026 Seoul Tourism Guidebook》 Web Edition — 5 Major Districts, Theme Courses, Culinary, and Hanok Complete Summary
story_seoul_visitseoul_guide.subtitle: Complete core 50-page official guidebook for Seoul's 5 major districts (Downtown, Central, Northeast, Northwest, Gangnam)
story_seoul_visitseoul_guide.address: 161 Sajik-ro, Jongno-gu, Seoul (Gyeongbokgung Palace, Bukchon, Namsan, Hangang Districts)
story_seoul_visitseoul_guide.pull_quote: Check out the 12MB, 50-page 《2026 Seoul Tourism Guidebook》 covering royal palaces, Hanyangdoseong Fortress Wall, museums, Hangang River, neighborhood alleys, food alleys, festivals, and practical info all in one web magazine.
paragraphs:
【CHAPTER 1 · Seoul's 5 Major Royal Palaces & Free Hanbok Admission Tips】
The first gateway to a Seoul trip consists of Gyeongbokgung, Changdeokgung, Changgyeonggung (09:00~21:00), Deoksugung, Gyeonghuigung, and Jongmyo Shrine, where 500 years of the Joseon Dynasty's history dwell. Visitors wearing Hanbok can enter all five royal palaces for free, and advance reservations for Changdeokgung's Secret Garden and Gyeongbokgung's nighttime viewing can be made at the Royal Palace and Tombs Center (royal.khs.go.kr).

【CHAPTER 2 · Downtown Fortress Wall & Hanyangdoseong Hiking】
Hanyangdoseong Fortress Wall Trail, a historical site connecting Seoul's ridges, offers sections tailored to your stamina level. Representative courses include the gentle walking-style Naksan Section (Hyehwamun to Heunginjimun, 2.1km, approx. 1 hr), the Namsan Section connecting to Namsan Park (4.2km, approx. 3 hrs), and the Baekak Section with exceptional ridge views (Changuimun to Hyehwamun, 4.7km, approx. 3 hrs).

【CHAPTER 3 · National Museums & Best Culture/Art Spaces】
The historic course centers around the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan (night opening Wed/Sat until 21:00), which houses about 430,000 artifacts including national treasures, the National Hangeul Museum, and the Seodaemun Prison History Hall. Contemporary art continues to the MMCA Seoul and Deoksugung, Seoul Museum of Art, Leeum Museum of Art, and Hongje Yuyeon, a public art space in the underground of Eugene Shopping Center along Hongjecheon Stream.

【CHAPTER 4 · 8 Hangang Parks & Urban Forest Healing】
Cycling, picnics, and water leisure unfold along the Hangang River, stretching from Yeouido, Banpo, Mangwon, Ichon, Jamwon, Ttukseom, and Jamsil Hangang Parks to Nodeul Island, a music complex cultural space. Top urban retreats include Seoul Forest, famous for its silver grass view at Wind Hill, World Cup Park, and Maeheon Citizens' Forest.

【CHAPTER 5 · Seoul's 5 Major Districts' Neighborhoods & Walkable Alleys】
The distinct characteristics of each district shine brightly: Central (Myeongdong, Euljiro, Namsan Oreumi, Dongdaemun), Central-North (Seochon Cafe Street, Bukchon Hanok Village with over 900 houses, Insadong, Daehangno), Northeast (Seongsu-shodak/Handmade Shoe Street, Cafe Street, Konkuk Univ. Common Ground), Northwest/Gangseo (Sangam, Hapjeong, Mangwon, Hongdae, Yeonnam, Mullae Creative Village, Hangdong Railroad), and Gangnam/Jamsil (Sinsa Garosu-gil, Apgujeong Rodeo, COEX Aquarium, Seokchon Lake).

【CHAPTER 6 · TASTY SEOUL Food Alleys, Old Shops & Seasonal Festivals】
Local soul foods like Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market, Jangchung-dong Jokbal (Pig's Trotters) Alley, and Ojangdong Hamheung Naengmyeon Street are rich alongside long-established shops and vegan restaurants. Seasonally, the Yeouido Spring Flower Festival in April, Hangang Festival in July–August, and Seoul Street Arts Festival & Seoul World Fireworks Festival in September–October adorn all of Seoul.

story_ebook_busan.source_book: Visit Busan Official Tourist Map & Local Culinary & Coastal Train Guidebook
story_ebook_busan.title: Busan Official Guide, Breathing with Blue Seas and Local Cuisine
story_ebook_busan.subtitle: Web edition from Haeundae Blue Line Park to old downtown culinary alleys
story_ebook_busan.pull_quote: Explore the breathtaking coastal train scenery and Busan's deep-rooted culinary history perfectly with the official tourism guidebook.
paragraphs:
【CHAPTER 1 · Landmark & History/Culture Core Course】
Your first step into Busan, South Korea's maritime capital, begins at the old Baekje Hospital carrying the historical breath of the old downtown, and Gwangbok-ro Fashion Street, a street of modern culture. Proceeding through Nampodong and Jagalchi Market, ascend Yongdusan Park to view Busan Port, and enjoy a thrilling aerial walk across the sea aboard the Songdo Marine Cable Car. Explore the colorful terraced houses and maze-like alleyways in nearby Gamcheon Culture Village to deeply understand Busan's modern and contemporary refugee capital history.

【CHAPTER 2 · Nature, Trekking & Drive Healing Route】
To fully enjoy Busan's magnificent coastal scenery, a coastal drive course starting from Haeundae Beach along the Mipo Railroad to Dalmaji-gil is ideal. Board the Haeundae Blue Line Park Beach Train at Cheongsapo to admire the blue East Sea, then head to Oryukdo Skywalk to feel the thrilling sensation of looking down at the waves spreading beneath the transparent glass floor. If you want urban nature, hike the Geumjeongsanseong North Gate trail and walk along Daecheoncheon Valley to fully recharge with fresh forest energy.

【CHAPTER 3 · Local Culinary, Traditional Market & Alley Tour】
Your culinary journey discovering Busan's deep local flavors begins at Bupyeong Kkangtong Market and Gukje Market's night market alleys. Taste fresh seafood and neat local dishes at Yun-ga-ne Shintoburi Bossam and Eoga Sushi, highly recommended by locals, and don't miss the fun of picking and eating Busan's representative soul foods like Milmyeon (wheat noodles), Dwaeji Gukbap (pork soup with rice), and Ssiat Hotteok (seed-filled pancakes). Finish a leisurely alley tour enjoying fragrant coffee and handmade desserts at a unique roastery cafe on Jeonpo Cafe Street.

【CHAPTER 4 · Night Views, Emotional Spots & Four-Season Festivals】
At dusk, Busan transforms into a dazzling night-view paradise; especially the high-rise skyscraper night views of Marine City viewed from Hwangnyeongsan Observatory and The Bay 101 are breathtaking. Spend a romantic night watching the Gwangdaegyo Bridge media art and weekend drone show at Gwangalli Beach. Diverse cultural festivals across the four seasons, including the Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) and Busan Fireworks Festival held every autumn, enrich the traveler's five senses.

【CHAPTER 5 · 1N2D Recommended Stay Route & Legal Accommodation/Transport Tips】
For a successful 1N2D Busan trip, we recommend linking a marine resort course centered around Haeundae and Gwangalli beaches on day one, with an old downtown history and culture course in Yeongdo and Nampodong on day two. Use KTO-designated excellent accommodations and safe tourist hotels located near Haeundae Beach and Busan Station, and travel conveniently using the Busan City Tour Bus (Taejongdae and Haeundae routes) and public transit passes.

story_ebook_daegu.source_book: Daegu Trip Road Official Tourist Guide Map & Modern Alley E-book
story_ebook_daegu.title: Daegu Trip Road, A City Hidden with Diverse Charms
story_ebook_daegu.subtitle: Luxury travel E-book web edition blending history, nature, and Daegu's 10 Flavors
story_ebook_daegu.pull_quote: Take a perfect local trip walking along the footsteps of modern alleys with the Daegu Trip Road official guide, enjoying Palgongsan Mountain's beautiful nature and the deep flavors of Daegu's 10 Flavors.
paragraphs:
【CHAPTER 1 · Landmark & History/Culture Core Course】
Following Daegu Jung-gu's Modern Alley Tour Course 2, tour the March 1st Independence Movement Road, Gyesan Catholic Church, and Lee Sang-hwa's Residence in order to vividly feel the breath of Korea's modern history. Next, move to Dongseongro Street of Youth, often called Daegu's Myeongdong, to enjoy shopping and modern culture and art, and savor the uniquely sweet-and-spicy cuisine at Bangogae Muchimhoe (Mixed Raw Fish/Mollusks) Alley, one of Daegu's 10 Flavors. Take a break at Gukchaebosang Movement Memorial Park, an oasis in the city, to discover Daegu's true charm where history and modernity coexist.

【CHAPTER 2 · Nature, Trekking & Drive Healing Route】
Ascend Palgongsan National Park, designated among Korea's 100 Best Tourist Spots, to find peace of mind while appreciating the tranquil scenery and grand giant Buddha of the millennium-old temple Donghwasan. Then head to Bisulsan Natural Recreation Forest, a famous attraction in southwestern Daegu, to comfortably view the mountain scenery where azalea colonies and silver grass create a spectacle via electric car. On your way down, restore your energy with hearty Hyunpung Centennial Native Chicken or Hyunpung Gomtang (Beef Bone Soup), and enjoy a leisurely cup of tea at an emotional cafe around Gachang Reservoir, famous for its driving course.

【CHAPTER 3 · Local Culinary, Traditional Market & Alley Tour】
Visit Daegu Seomyeon Market, Korea's largest traditional market, to taste diverse street foods like Napjak Mandu (flat dumplings), Ssiat Hotteok, and Kaljebi (knife-cut noodles and sujebi soup), fully experiencing the vibrant energy of tradition. Explore Daegu's unique food ecosystem connecting Nammun Market and Bangchon Market, and purchase Mayak Bread (whole corn bread) at Milbat Bakery, one of Daegu's top 3 bakeries, adding a special culinary joy. In the evening, visit Pyeonghwa Market's Dakttongjib (Chicken Gizzard) Alley to taste crispy fried gizzards paired with cold local beer for the essence of Daegu's nightlife.

【CHAPTER 4 · Night Views, Emotional Spots & Four-Season Festivals】
Ascend E-World and 83 Tower, the symbols of Daegu, to spend a romantic time viewing the brilliant panoramic night scenery of all of Daegu. Climb Apsan Observatory via cable car to view the New Year's sunrise or urban night views, and join nationwide festival excitement like the Bisulsan Azalea Cultural Festival in spring and Daegu Chimac Festival in summer. Move to Suseongmot Lake Resort to watch the colorful video music fountain shows held every night, and stroll along the promenade built around the lake to complete a romantic Daegu night.

【CHAPTER 5 · 1N2D Recommended Stay Route & Legal Accommodation/Transport Tips】
On day one, arrive at Dongdaegu Station and efficiently handle the central downtown course taking the Daegu City Tour Bus through Modern Alleys and Seomyeon Market to Suseongmot Lake night views. On day two, enjoy a comfortable stay at a pleasant Hanok stay at the foot of Palgongsan Mountain or an excellent accommodation in Dong-gu or Jung-gu, and wrap up your schedule with a hiking trip to Palgongsan Gatbawi. Actively utilizing Daegu Subway Lines 1–3, Daeguro Pay, and Daegu Tour Pass makes your local trip more economical and smart.

story_ebook_incheon.title: History and Scenery Sculpted by Time: Incheon and Ganghwa Island Cultural Travel
story_ebook_incheon.subtitle: A pilgrimage to Ganghwa-do's dondae (fortified watchtowers) and a culinary exploration with Incheon's official guidebook
story_ebook_incheon.pull_quote: Ganghwa-do's Samnangseong Fortress, Janggotdondae Fortified Watchtower, and rich local cuisine—steeped in history and the traces of time—will make travelers pause and stay awhile.
paragraphs:
【CHAPTER 1 · Representative Landmarks & Core History & Culture Course】
Begin your historical exploration at Ganghwa Samnangseong Fortress, shrouded in the legend of Dangun Wanggeom, and continue to Ganghwa Goseong and Ganghwa Sanseong Fortress, which served as the temporary capital of Goryeo. Feel thousands of years of breath as you overlook the West Sea and the Han River estuary from Gapgotdondae Fortified Watchtower and Yeonmijeong Pavilion, key military strongholds of the Joseon Dynasty. Cross over to Gyodong-do Island, stroll through Hwagae-gweongwon Garden and the classic Gyodong Hyanggyo Confucian School, and experience a profound resonance as if traveling through a time slip.

【CHAPTER 2 · Nature, Trekking, & Driving Healing Route】
Connecting Janggotdondae, renowned for its West Sea sunset, and Seokmodo Marine, the West Coast driving course presents breathtaking scenery where vast tidal flats and the sea harmonize. Ascend Seokmodo Bomunsa Temple and gaze at the refreshing ocean view beneath Nunnseopbawi (Eyebrow Rock) to heal your mind and body fatigued from daily life. The forest trekking trail along the foothills of Manisan Chamseongdan Altar fills you with phytoncides and gifts a healthy time of recharge.

【CHAPTER 3 · Local Culinary, Traditional Market, & Alley Tour】
Following the resonance of history exploration, taste baeng-engi muchim (spiced seasoned mudskipper) and jeotgukgalbi (pork ribs stewed in salted shrimp) at Ganghwa Pungmul Market to add joy to your travel. Wander through the alleys of Daeryong Market on Gyodong-do Island, enjoy ssanghwacha (traditional herbal tea) that stirs old memories, and fragrant snacks made with Ganghwa ginseng. To conclude your journey, savor trendy dining and coffee culture in the sophisticated culinary spots and cafe streets of Cheongna International City.

【CHAPTER 4 · Night Views, Emotional Spots, & Four-Season Festivals】
An evening tour where the modern architecture of the Incheon Open Port Street blends with soft lighting completes a romantic night. The night scenery created by Incheon Port's night sea viewed from Wolmi Sea Train and the skyscrapers of Songdo Central Park stimulates urban sensibility. The Ganghwa Goryeo Cultural Festival held every autumn and the Goryungsan Mountain Azalea Festival in full bloom every spring add reasons to visit all year round.

【CHAPTER 5 · 1N2D Recommended Staying Route & Legal Accommodation & Transportation Tips】
On Day 1, finish exploring the history of Ganghwa-eup and Gyodong-do Daeryong Market, then melt away fatigue at a Seokmodo hot spring resort or an ocean-view pension. On Day 2, the ideal route is moving to Cheongna and Songdo to enjoy sophisticated brunch and a stroll through Central Park. For a safe and comfortable trip, use Incheon-certified accommodations, and for the Ganghwa and Gyodong areas, renting a car or utilizing the Incheon City Tour bus is recommended considering public transit dispatch intervals.

story_ebook_gwangju.title: Strolling through Gwangju, Bitgoeul: Namdo's City of Arts Where Art and Nature Breathe
story_ebook_gwangju.subtitle: A Gwangju local travel web edition where Mudeungsan's scenic beauty and modern culture and art coexist
story_ebook_gwangju.pull_quote: From the pristine nature of Mudeungsan National Park to the emotion-filled Art Street and Chungjang-ro, discover the deep and colorful cultural heritage embraced by Bitgoeul Gwangju.
paragraphs:
【CHAPTER 1 · Representative Landmarks & Core History & Culture Course】
Starting with the National Asian Culture Center (ACC) and encompassing the 5·18 Democracy Square and Geumnam-ro, this walking tour is the essential starting point for a Gwangju trip. After reflecting on the history of the May 18 Democratic Uprising at Jeonil Building 245's rooftop garden and 10th-floor exhibition hall, move to Yangnim-dong History and Culture Village, steeped in modern historical and cultural sentiment, to explore missionary Eugene Bell's house and Penguin Village. In the evening, browse traditional crafts in Art Street, the center of Namdo art, and conclude the first day's schedule by tasting deep-flavored yukjeon (pan-fried battered beef) and oritang (duck stew) at a nearby restaurant.

【CHAPTER 2 · Nature, Trekking, & Driving Healing Route】
To fully enjoy the gorgeous nature of Mudeungsan National Park, designated as a UNESCO Global Geopark, start from the Jeungsimsa District and trek toward the columnar jointing groups of Seoseokdae and Ipseokdae. On the descent, visit the millennial ancient temple Wonhyosa to gain peace of mind and body amidst the serene mountain temple scenery, and appreciate the beautiful forest paths around Jungmeorijae and Pungamje along the Mudeungsan driving route. After the hike, heartily fill your empty stomach with warm boribap (barley rice) set meal and dotoriguk (acorn jelly) in the shopping street at the entrance of Jeungsimsa Temple.

【CHAPTER 3 · Local Culinary, Traditional Market, & Alley Tour】
Enjoy a retro-sensibility alley tour by browsing youth startup shops modernly reinterpreted and gukbap (rice soup) alleys preserving old sentiments at Gwangju 1913 Songjeong Station Market. Next, visit Yangdong Market to experience Namdo's true local delicacies with all five senses, including savory whole fried chicken, pungent hongeo-samhap (fermented skate, pork, and kimchi), and spicy chicken feet. Conclude the gourmet trip by finishing a bowl of unique and rich perilla seed duck stew at Oritang Street lined up along the Gwangju Stream, enjoying the ultimate gastronomic joy.

【CHAPTER 4 · Night Views, Emotional Spots, & Four-Season Festivals】
Spend a romantic time at dusk climbing Sajik Park Observatory Tower to view Gwangju downtown's brilliant night scenery and Mudeungsan's silhouette at a glance. Visit the Jungoe Park Culture Belt and Gwangju Biennale Exhibition Hall to appreciate world-class contemporary art works, and join the festive heat of the Gwangju Chungjang Festival and Gwangju Biennale held every season. The nightscape lighting around Bitgoeul Citizen's Culture Center and Kim Dae-jung Convention Center adds joy to night walks.

【CHAPTER 5 · 1N2D Recommended Staying Route & Legal Accommodation & Transportation Tips】
For Day 1, arrive at KTX Songjeong Station and explore the culture and art course connecting Yangnim-dong and ACC. For Day 2, a 1-night 2-day schedule consisting of Mudeungsan hiking and 1913 Songjeong Station Market gourmet exploration is ideal. For lodging, it is convenient to use a business hotel in Sangmu District or a clean Hanok guesthouse near the National Asian Culture Center. In Gwangju downtown, utilizing Subway Line 1 and the City Tour Bus allows you to move to major tourist spots quickly and comfortably.

story_ebook_daejeon.subtitle: A sweet bakery pilgrimage and healing walking trails enjoyed in the Republic of Korea's capital of science
story_ebook_daejeon.address: 100 Dunsan-ro, Seo-gu, Daejeon (based on Daejeon City Hall)
story_ebook_daejeon.pull_quote: A special intellectual and culinary journey to Daejeon, the trendiest gourmet city in the country and where the history of South Korea's science and technology breathes.
paragraphs:
【CHAPTER 1 · Representative Landmarks & Core History & Culture Course】
Start your trip by visiting Expo Science Park and Hanbit Tower, symbols of Daejeon, the capital of science in South Korea, to watch dazzling media facades and musical fountains. Next, walk along the Veterans' Hiking Trail at Daejeon National Cemetery, where you can feel the footsteps of South Korea's modern history, and Uam Historic Park, full of traditional fragrance, to enjoy the serene atmosphere. If you are with children, you can fully encompass Daejeon Solomon Law Park, where you can easily and funly experience law and judicial procedures, and the cultural and arts cluster around Daejeon Arts Center.

【CHAPTER 2 · Nature, Trekking, & Driving Healing Route】
Experience true healing amidst fresh phytoncides by walking barefoot on Bwomunsan Happy Forest Trail and Gaeksusan Red Clay Path, which boast green forests in the city center. Daecheongho Obaek-ri-gil, running along Daecheongho Lake, is perfect as a driving course, offering the leisure of sipping a fragrant coffee while viewing the lake. The footbath experience area around Yuseong Hot Spring Station is the ultimate healing spot that completely washes away travel fatigue and restores vitality.

【CHAPTER 3 · Local Culinary, Traditional Market, & Alley Tour】
True to its reputation as a nationwide 'bakery pilgrimage' mecca, taste fried soboro and chive bread at Sungsimdang Main Branch, and explore the bakery alley around Daejeon Station and Eunhaeng-dong. Feel the lively atmosphere and warm hospitality of a traditional market with all your body by tasting spicy kalguksu (knife-cut noodles), stir-fried webfoot octopus, and old-style whole fried chicken at Daejeon Jungang Market. Fill a healthy and special meal with cool and savory acorn jelly rice soup (dotori mukbap) in Guguk's traditional acorn jelly village.

【CHAPTER 4 · Night Views, Emotional Spots, & Four-Season Festivals】
Spend an emotional time visiting Hanbit Tower Water Wave Square at dusk to enjoy the passionate atmosphere of a food truck festival along with Daejeon's brilliant night view. The Daejeon Science Festival and Daejeon Kalguksu Festival held every autumn around Daejeon Stream and the original downtown area present Daejeon's unique identity and colorful attractions. Festivals showcasing unique charms every season, such as the Daejeon Expo Citizen's Plaza Outdoor Ice Rink and Yuseong Hot Spring Cultural Festival, welcome travelers.

【CHAPTER 5 · 1N2D Recommended Staying Route & Legal Accommodation & Transportation Tips】
On Day 1, we recommend a fruitful route: arriving at Daejeon Station, going through Jungang Market and Eunhaeng-dong bakery pilgrimage, and appreciating the night views of Expo Science Park and Hanbit Tower. On Day 2, trek the Gyeryoksan Red Clay Path and drive along Daecheongho Lake before returning home. For accommodation, it is convenient to use a premium hotel within the Yuseong Hot Spring Special Zone, a business hotel in the center of Dunsan-dong, or a clean guesthouse near Daejeon Station. Connecting Daejeon Subway Line 1, City Tour Bus, and Tashu (public bicycles) allows you to smart and eco-friendly explore every corner of Daejeon.

story_ebook_ulsan.title: Ulsan Magazine Travel: A City Where the Blue Sea and Mysterious Whale Dreams Breathe
story_ebook_ulsan.subtitle: A Healing Web Edition Spanning from Jangsaepo Whale Culture Special Zone to the Ridges of the Yeongnam Alps
story_ebook_ulsan.pull_quote: Turn the page of an unforgettable journey in Ulsan, where the dynamism of South Korea's industrial capital coexists with the clear blue Taehwagang River and the mystery of ecology.
paragraphs:
【CHAPTER 1 · Representative Landmarks & Core History & Culture Course】
Experience the vivid history of a former whaling forward base at the Jangsaepo Whale Culture Special Zone, and enjoy a romantic adventure riding the Whale Sea Travel Ship across the blue East Sea to meet pods of oceanic dolphins. Next, visit the Daegokcheon Stream heritage site, home to National Treasure No. 285 Bangudae Petroglyphs and Cheonjeon-ri Petroglyphs, to deeply feel the cultural breath of prehistoric Ulsan. At Taehwagang National Garden, stroll under the cool bamboo shade of Simnidaeut Forest and capture unforgettable memories in photos under the mystical night illumination of the Milky Way Street.

【CHAPTER 2 · Nature, Trekking & Drive Healing Route】
Immerse yourself in a trekking experience wandering through the silver grass plains of Gajisan and Sinbulsan Mountains amid the grand, breathtaking scenery of the Yeongnam Alps, listed among South Korea's top 100 mountains. After catching the brilliant sunrise—the earliest on the Korean Peninsula—at Ganjeolgot Cape, find leisure along with the sound of waves by driving the Gangdong Judong Pebble Beach course stretching along the coastline. We also recommend exploring the wide green spaces, zoo, and botanical gardens of Ulsan Grand Park to relax amidst the comfort provided by urban nature.

【CHAPTER 3 · Local Gastronomy, Traditional Markets & Alley Tour】
Visit Ulsan Jungang Market, a representative traditional market in Ulsan, to feel the lively local atmosphere, and broaden your culinary horizons by tasting regional specialties like whale meat suyuk (boiled slices) and yukhoe (tartare) at the Whale Meat Specialized Street. At Eonyang Bulgogi Specialized Street located in Eonyang-eup, you can heartily enjoy traditional Eonyang bulgogi with a subtle charcoal grill aroma made by grilling high-quality Korean beef on a wire rack, paired with minari (water dropwort) samgyeopsal. Pairing regional seafood dishes with refreshing Ulsan raw makgeolli at the Taehwagang riverside dining district doubles the joy of your trip.

【CHAPTER 4 · Night Views, Emotional Spots & Four-Season Festivals】
Breathtaking views of the East Coast seen from the hanging bridges of Taehwagang National Garden and Daewangam Park offer charms that completely differ between day and night. Especially at night, the media art 'Ilsan Fantasy' unfolds a feast of light around Daewangam Park. Climb up the Ulsan Bridge Observatory to take in the splendid night views of Jangsaepo Port and Ulsan's industrial complex at one glance, and appreciate the dynamic nightscape of the city. Vibrant festivals unfolding across all four seasons, such as the Taehwagang National Garden Spring Flower Festival in spring and the Ulsan Whale Festival in autumn, add excitement to your Ulsan trip.

【CHAPTER 5 · 2-Day 1-Night Recommended Stay Route & Legal Accommodation & Transportation Tips】
For Day 1, we recommend arriving at KTX Ulsan Station, enjoying the Yeongnam Alps and an Eonyang bulgogi lunch, passing through Taehwagang National Garden and Simnidaeut Forest, and staying at a downtown hotel. For Day 2, the most fulfilling itinerary involves sequentially touring the Jangsaepo Whale Culture Special Zone, Daewangam Park, and Ganjeolgot Cape before heading back home along the East Coast. Using the Ulsan City Tour Bus makes it convenient to travel to major tourist spots, and it is smart to book clean tourist hotels and registered pensions near the Taehwagang riverside and Jangsaepo in advance.

story_ebook_sejong.subtitle: Sejong · A Smart Healing Web Edition Where Nature and City Harmonize
story_ebook_sejong.pull_quote: Experience a vibrant downtown healing journey encompassing the National Sejong Arboretum and Geumgang Pedestrian Bridge (Eungdari Bridge) in Sejong, the center of South Korea.
paragraphs:
【CHAPTER 1 · Representative Landmarks & Core History & Culture Course】
This course connects the Government Complex Sejong Rooftop Garden—where you can take in the center of South Korea at a glance—with Eungdari Bridge (Geumgang Pedestrian Bridge), South Korea's first double-deck pedestrian bridge. After exploring the grand-scale Presidential Archives, you can comfortably travel on foot or by vehicle to the National Hangul Museum, where you can feel the identity of a Hangeul cultural city named after King Sejong. For lunch, recharge your travel energy at nearby restaurants by tasting Sejong's light local delicacies such as freshwater shrimp spicy stew (minmulsaewu-maeuntang) or Korean beef bulgogi.

【CHAPTER 2 · Nature, Trekking & Drive Healing Route】
Indulge in a fresh green relaxation while strolling through the four-season greenhouses and various themed gardens at the National Sejong Arboretum, the largest urban-type arboretum in South Korea. At the adjoining Sejong Lake Park, you can enjoy light trekking along the Floating Stage Island and Wind Hill while admiring open waterfront scenery. Extend your drive to Bear Tree Park in Jeondong-myeon, where you can walk among Asiatic black bears and a 100,000-pyeong arboretum, completing perfect healing amidst nature.

【CHAPTER 3 · Local Gastronomy, Traditional Markets & Alley Tour】
Visit Jochiwon Traditional Market to encounter Sejong's living traditions and warm hospitality, fully experiencing the lively atmosphere of its 5-day periodic market. Enjoy an alley gastronomic exploration tasting market specialties such as multi-generational chicken tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), savory padak (green onion fried chicken), and desserts made from fresh peaches grown in Sejong. Record precious memories of your Sejong trip over a leisurely cup of coffee at emotional cafe streets in Dajeong-dong and Naseong-dong, lined with local cafes.

【CHAPTER 4 · Night Views, Emotional Spots & Four-Season Festivals】
As dusk falls, ascend Eungdari Bridge, which dyes the Geumgang River in silver, and spend a romantic time appreciating dazzling media art and fantastic night views. During the Sejong Festival period every autumn, you can fully enjoy Sejong's unique festive atmosphere through fireworks shows and various Hangeul cultural experience programs unfolding around the Geumgang Lake Park area. The Bangchukcheon Music Fountain Square, where you can leave life-shot photos against the backdrop of a beautiful night view, is also an unmissable emotional spot.

【CHAPTER 5  · 2-Day 1-Night Recommended Stay Route & Legal Accommodation & Transportation Tips】
We recommend a fulfilling 2-day 1-night itinerary: Day 1 involves walking through the National Sejong Arboretum and Lake Park followed by viewing the night view of Eungdari Bridge; Day 2 continues with visiting Bear Tree Park and touring Jochiwon Traditional Market. For lodging, it is convenient to book in advance a business hotel near the Government Complex Sejong boasting clean facilities or a nature-friendly Hanok stay in Janggun-myeon. Utilizing BRT (Bus Rapid Transit) circulating downtown Sejong and 'Ooulling' public bicycles allows you to enjoy an eco-friendly yet economical urban trip.

story_ebook_gyeonggi.title: Gyeonggi-do's Diverse Charming Travel Where History and Nature Breathe
story_ebook_gyeonggi.subtitle: An Urban Healing Local Course Departing with Official Guidebooks
story_ebook_gyeonggi.pull_quote: From Hwahongmun Gate embracing a thousand years of history to Yuldong Park and Golpo Jungang Park acting as urban oases, begin a diverse local trip guided by Gyeonggi-do's official guidebook.
paragraphs:
【CHAPTER 1 · Representative Landmarks & Core History & Culture Course】
Walking along the grand fortress walls of Suwon Hwaseong Fortress, Hwahongmun Gate and Banghwasuryujeong Pavilion are top historical landmarks highlighting the harmony of Joseon-dynasty architectural beauty and nature. Next, explore Suwon Hwaseong Haenggung Palace, designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site, to vividly experience diverse historical cultures imbued with the reform ideology and filial piety of King Jeongjo of Joseon. Food comes before sightseeing—add culinary joy by tasting crispy Suwon Wanggalbi-tongdak (fried chicken seasoned with king galbi flavor) fried in a traditional cauldron at nearby Suwon Tongdak Street.

【CHAPTER 2 · Nature, Trekking & Drive Healing Route】
Walking along the clear valleys and green forest paths of Gwanggyosan Mountain in Suwon offers a healing time that completely washes away daily fatigue within the city. Next, move to Seongnam to enjoy leisurely nature strolling along the wide lakes and walking paths of Yuldong Park and Jungang Park, and experience the drive course around the Namhansanseong Rotary. You can feel the tranquility provided by nature with all your senses amidst lush forests and open scenery.

【CHAPTER 3 · Local Gastronomy, Traditional Markets & Alley Tour】
Visit Suwon Nammun Market and Jidong Market to vividly experience foods from diverse local traditional markets, such as sundae gopchang stir-fry (blood sausage and pork intestines) and old-school fried chicken. After strolling through the charming alleys near Golpo Jungang Park in Gimpo, it is recommended to enjoy a full-course meal made with rice cooked from Gimpo Golden Rice and fresh local agricultural products. You can enjoy the lively atmosphere of a traditional market alongside browsing crafts touched by local artisans.

【CHAPTER 4 · Night Views, Emotional Spots & Four-Season Festivals】
After sunset, the Suwon Hwaseong Fortress and Banghwasuryujeong Pavilion areas are famous as fantastic emotional spots that create antique nightscapes with added soft lighting. Visiting during the Suwon Hwaseong Cultural Festival every autumn allows the whole family to enjoy diverse festival programs together, such as magnificent night procession reenactments and traditional performances. Leave romantic life-shot photos against the backdrop of Seongnam Yuldong Park's night fountain show and sparkling urban night views.

【CHAPTER 5 · 2-Day 1-Night Recommended Stay Route & Legal Accommodation & Transportation Tips】
On Day 1, explore Suwon Hwaseong Fortress, Haenggung-dong Cafe Street, and traditional markets, then enjoy a comfortable stay at a verified tourist hotel or clean Hanok guesthouse near Suwon Hwaseong Fortress. On Day 2, complete your route with an itinerary moving to Gimpo Golpo Jungang Park and Seongnam Yuldong Park to savor leisure amidst nature. Equipped with metropolitan subway lines and metropolitan bus routes, you can travel conveniently using public transportation alone, and utilizing the Gyeonggi Tour Pass allows you to use major tourist spots and cafes even more affordably.

story_ebook_chungbuk.title: A Healing Journey in Chungbuk Where Millennium History and Pristine Nature Breathe
story_ebook_chungbuk.subtitle: A local trip from the tranquil scenery of Haneuljae Pass to Angseong Hot Springs that melt away fatigue
story_ebook_chungbuk.pull_quote: We propose a perfect punctuation mark to heal your body and mind with Chungju's savory local food and hot springs, washing away daily fatigue while walking the ancient paths of Poamsan Mountain and Haneuljae embracing magnificent mountain ranges.
paragraphs:
【CHAPTER 1 · Representative Landmarks & History/Culture Core Course】
A Chungbuk journey embracing a millennium of history begins amidst the natural scenery of Chungju Haneuljae, South Korea's oldest mountain pass, and the majestic Poamsan Mountain. You can enjoy an in-depth historical excursion by exploring historically rich cultural properties imbued with the breaths of Baekje, Silla, and Joseon, such as Mireukdaewonji Temple Site, Danyang's magnificent Dodam Sambong Peaks, and Guinsa Temple. The cruise tour along the Chungju Hoban (Lake Chungju) is the ultimate history and culture course to experience the breathtaking scenery created by jade-colored waves and bizarre rocks up close.

【CHAPTER 2 · Nature, Trekking & Drive Healing Route】
The lush forest paths of Woraksan National Park and the driving course along Lake Cheongpungho form the ultimate healing route to soothe your mind and body fatigued from daily life. Walking along the Sobaeksan Jalrak-gil (Footpath), you can feel deep comfort delivered by the sound of clear valley water and forests full of phytoncides. Stop by the Angseong Carbonated Hot Spring District to completely wash away your fatigue with refreshing carbonated hot spring baths, and enjoy a leisurely stroll and camping sentiment at Mokgye Solbat Natural Rest Area.

【CHAPTER 3 · Local Gastronomy, Traditional Market & Alley Tour】
Jecheon Ekjeon-yonghan Market and Chungju Jayu Market are visited for an alley tour where you discover the true local flavors of Chungbuk amidst the warm hospitality of vendors. Jecheon's deep and savory natural sirakguk (dried radish greens soup), herbal bossam fitting for the land of medicinal herbs, and fresh grilled Hanwoo beef that melts in your mouth double the joy of travel. Diverse local foods tasted at Danyang Gugyeong Market, such as black garlic dakgangjeong (sweet crispy fried chicken) and olgaengigukbap (freshwater snail soup with rice), perfectly satisfy gourmands' five senses.

【CHAPTER 4 · Night Views, Emotional Spots & Four-Season Festivals】
Emotional spots await where you can enjoy thrilling sensations and panoramic views of the Namhangang River while walking along Danyang Mancheonha Skywalk and Danyanggang Zandogil (Cliff Trail). The brilliant sunsets and splendid night views seen from Uirimji Reservoir in Chungju and the upper pavilion of Cheongpungho Lake Cable Car leave unforgettable life photos. Enjoy the charms of all four seasons: the Jecheon Cheongpungho Cherry Blossom Festival in spring, water play in Goesan Myeongdeok Valley in summer, Danyang Sobaeksan azaleas and autumn foliage in autumn, and Chungju Suanbo Hot Springs Festival in winter.

【CHAPTER 5 · Recommended 1N2D Stay Route & Legal Accommodation/Transportation Tips】
Day 1 consists of trekking Haneuljae in Chungju, exploring Mireukdaewonji Temple Site, relieving fatigue at Angseong Hot Springs, and spending a comfortable night at a cozy hanok stay near Lake Chungju or a safe condo/pension registered under the Tourism Promotion Act. Day 2 completes a fruitful 1-night 2-day stay route of touring Jecheon Uirimji Reservoir and Cheongpungho Lake Cable Car, tasting local food, and returning home. You can access quickly and conveniently from the metropolitan area by using KTX-Eum and Jungbu Naeryuk Expressway, and an even more economical trip is possible by utilizing the Chungbuk City Tour bus.

story_ebook_chungnam.pull_quote: Experience the deep charms of Chungnam with the official guidebook, from the thousand-year history of Buyeo's Baekje culture to the breathtaking sunsets of the west coast and the serene landscapes of Asan Oeam Folk Village.
paragraphs:
【CHAPTER 1 · Landmark & History-Culture Core Course】
A 2-day, 1-night historical tour starting at Gongju Gongsanseong Fortress and Songsan-ri Tombs (King Muryeong's Royal Tomb) to experience the essence of Baekje culture, followed by Buyeo Nakhwaam Cliff and Gungnamji Lotus Pond. Admire the sophisticated brick tomb style of King Muryeong's Tomb, hike up Busosanseong Fortress, and overlook the breathtaking views of the Baengmagang River from Nakhwaam, tied to Baekje's final tales. In the evening, savor lotus leaf rice set meals packed with Buyeo's specialty chestnuts to fully feel the antique breath of Baekje.

【CHAPTER 2 · Nature, Trekking & Drive Healing Route】
A healing course driving along the beautiful coastline of Anmyeondo Island in Taean to admire the sunset at Kkotji Beach's Grandmother and Grandfather Rocks, trekking the pure green cherry blossom road at Seosan Gaheimsam Temple and Seohairang-gil Course 60. Pass by coastal driving courses embracing the cool West Sea, and encounter the wonders of nature at the Seosan Cheonsuman Migratory Bird Habitat. Stroll through the Seocheon Sinseongni Reed Bed spread along the Geumgang River's water currents and enjoy a moment of contemplation in the autumn breeze.

【CHAPTER 3 · Local Food, Traditional Market & Alley Tour】
A gourmet tour tasting Bulgogi and noodles at Yesan Traditional Market continuing Yesan's heritage, and enjoying fresh West Sea grilled clams and raw shirasu (silchihoe) near Dangjin Sapgyoho Sea Park. Sequentially visit Hongseong Gwangcheon Salted Shrimp Market and Boryeong Central Market to explore regional side dishes and salted seafood full of authentic local flavors. Treat yourself to local beer made from Yesan apples and apple pie as a dessert, and soak in the vibrant energy of local markets where tradition meets modernity.

【CHAPTER 4 · Night Views, Emotional Spots & Four-Season Festivals】
Experience Chungnam's representative global festivals such as the Boryeong Mud Festival and Geumsan World Ginseng Festival, while enjoying the night opening of Hyungchungsa Shrine blending Asan's brilliant history with lights and Pinnacle Land's fireworks festival. Capture the picture of a lifetime under the night sky of Nam-myeon, Taean, where millions of LED lights create a fantastic night view at the Taean Light Festival. Seasonal events like the Gongju Seokjangni Paleolithic Festival and Buyeo Seodong Lotus Festival captivate travelers throughout the year.

【CHAPTER 5 · 2D1N Recommended Stay & Legal Accommodation/Transportation Tips】
A 2-day, 1-night stay-type course exploring Baekje ruins in Gongju and Buyeo on the first day, passing through the Independence Hall of Korea in Cheonan, and melting away fatigue at Asan Onyang Hot Springs. For accommodations, book safe and legal tourist lodgings such as traditional old houses in the Gongju Hanok Village or Yesan Resom Resort for a refreshing rest. Using the West Gold Train (G-Train) and Chungnam City Tour Bus allows you to conveniently connect major attractions without a rental car.

story_ebook_gyeongnam.pull_quote: Meet the essence of Gyeongnam travel full of nature and romance along the Island Highway that perfectly connects the hidden islands and seas of the South Coast.
paragraphs:
【CHAPTER 1 · Representative Landmarks & History/Culture Core Course】
A course exploring Geoje Oedo Botania's exotic marine garden and Windy Hill, passing through Tongyeong Cable Car and Underwater Tunnel where you can overlook the blue sea of Mireukdo Island in Tongyeong at a glance. By linking Hansando Jeseungdang, the historical site of the Imjin War, and Geoje POW Camp Historic Park, you can reflect on the deep historical and cultural value of the South Coast. On-site, we recommend an experience enjoying traditional flavors by tasting Chungmu Gimbap and Honey Bread, the symbols of Tongyeong.

【CHAPTER 2 · Nature, Trekking & Drive Healing Route】
A fantastic coastal driving course connecting Sacheon Sea Cable Car, Namhae German Village, and Changseon-Samcheonpo Bridge where you can feel the essence of the South Coast Island Highway. Trekking along the terraced rice paddies of Namhae Borimam Temple and Darangyi Village provides the ultimate healing point to cure mind and body tired from daily life. You can fully enjoy the sound of blue waves of Namhae with a leisurely cup of tea at an ocean-view emotional cafe encountered during the drive.

【CHAPTER 3 · Local Gastronomy, Traditional Market & Alley Tour】
Experience vibrant local culture by visiting Tongyeong Jungang Market and Namhae Traditional Market where you can fully enjoy fresh seafood of the South Coast. Fresh tot gimbap (hijiki rice rolls) and grilled sea eel tasted in Sacheon, and Namhae's local food, anchovy ssambap (wrapped anchovies), are essential courses captivating gourmands' tastes. You can feel the warm affection of local residents by strolling through Tongyeong Dongpirang Mural Village and Seho Market embracing charming alleyways.

【CHAPTER 4 · Night Views, Emotional Spots & Four-Season Festivals】
Tongyeong DPNURI's mysterious digital night lighting show, Jinjuseong Fortress night view, and the sunset of Mulgeon-ri Windbreak Forest in Namhae are representative night view spots beautifully decorating the night of the South Coast. Diverse festivals are held all year round, such as Jinhae Gunhangje Festival and Sacheon Waryong Cultural Festival in spring, Geoje Sea-to-World Festival in summer, and Jinju Namgang Yudeung (Lantern) Festival and Namhae-gak Culture & Arts Platform in autumn. Lanterns decorating the night sky and splendid fireworks present unforgettable memories of the trip.

【CHAPTER 5 · Recommended 1N2D Stay Route & Legal Accommodation/Transportation Tips】
A perfect 1-night 2-day stay-type driving route where you tour Tongyeong Mireukdo and Jungang Market on the first day, stay at an ocean-view pension by the sea, and pass through Namhae German Village and Borimam Temple to Sacheon on the second day. You can take a comfortable rest by pre-booking safe and pleasant legal accommodation facilities and hanok stays certified by Gyeongsangnam-do. To safely traverse the South Coast Island Highway, utilize the transportation tip of starting from Sacheon Airport and Jinju Station when using a rental car.

story_ebook_jeju.pull_quote: Experience the true charm of Jeju, where the blue sea, mysterious volcanic cones (oreums), and diverse local delicacies blend together, deeply with the official guidebook.
paragraphs:
[CHAPTER 1 · Representative Landmarks & History/Culture Core Course]
Starting with the magnificent volcanic landscape of Seongsan Ilchubong Peak, this history and culture exploration course connects the coastal scenery of Seopjikoji and the Jeju Haenyeo Museum. You can deeply understand Jeju's female diver (haenyeo) culture and take your first step into the trip by tasting fresh sea urchin soup with rice (seonggae-gukbap) and grilled black pork nearby. It is composed of a route to feel the value of the UNESCO World Natural Heritage with your whole body.

[CHAPTER 2 · Nature, Trekking & Driving Healing Route]
After enjoying a drive along the Aewol Coastal Road with unfolding emerald-sea views, this is a healing trekking course where you can fully enjoy phytoncide at Yongnuni Oreum or Saryeoni Forest Path. While walking along Olle Trail Course 7, the lyrical scenery of the Jeju sea and stone wall paths unfolds. At the intermediate rest stop, you can enjoy refreshing ade made with Jeju tangerines and carrot cake.

[CHAPTER 3 · Local Gastronomy, Traditional Markets & Alley Tour]
This is a local gourmet alley tour satisfying all five senses, centered around Jeju Dongmun Market and Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market. You can vividly experience traditional Jeju tastes such as boiled pork slices (dombe-gogi), pork noodles (gogi-guksu), and omegi rice cakes, and it is optimal for shopping for souvenirs in the charming old downtown alleys of Jeju where cute gift shops gather. You can catch a glimpse of genuine Jeju life amidst the lively warmth of local merchants.

[CHAPTER 4 · Night Views, Emotional Spots & Four-Season Festivals]
Along with indoor media art emotional spots like Bunker de Lumières and Arte Museum, this is a romantic schedule to appreciate the night view of Jeju Port harmonizing with the night sea. You can meet diverse festivals across four seasons, from the Canola Flower Festival in spring, Hallim Park Lotus Festival in summer, Silver Grass Festival in autumn, to Hallasan Snow Mountain Festival in winter. At night, you can take a relaxing break at an emotional café near Hyeopjae Beach.

[CHAPTER 5 · 1N2D Recommended Stay Route & Legal Accommodation/Transportation Tips]
This is an efficient 1-night 2-day packed stay route connecting the eastern region (Seongsan, Udo) on the first day and the western region (Hyeopjae, Aewol) on the second day. For a safe trip, thoroughly check safe legal accommodations, rental cars, and public transportation usage tips certified by the Jeju Tourism Organization. Making the Jeju Airport Integrated Tourist Information Center your first stop to download the latest E-book guidebook will complete an even more perfect journey.

spot_ev_3107059.title: 2026 Sungnyemun Gate Guard Duty Ceremony
spot_ev_3107059.overview: The 'Sungnyemun Gate Guard Duty Ceremony', which guards Sungnyemun Gate, is officially closed on Mondays and operates daily from 10:00 to 15:40, excluding Mondays. Guard duty (Pasu) refers to defending the capital city wall and is one of the important military ceremonies of the Joseon Dynasty. Defending the capital city wall was a critical issue during the Joseon era, especially emerging as a serious problem after experiencing the Japanese Invasions of Korea and the Manchu War during the reign of King Seonjo. The guard duty ceremony is a Joseon-era military ceremony connecting the opening and closing of the city gates at Injeong and Paru with night patrol ceremonies, holding a position and role among the central military systems as important as guarding the royal palace.

paragraphs: The 'Sungnyemun Gate Guard Duty Ceremony', which guards Sungnyemun Gate, is officially closed on Mondays and operates daily from 10:00 to 15:40, excluding Mondays. Guard duty (Pasu) refers to defending the capital city wall and is one of the important military ceremonies of the Joseon Dynasty. Defending the capital city wall was a critical issue during the Joseon era, especially emerging as a serious problem after experiencing the Japanese Invasions of Korea and the Manchu War during the reign of King Seonjo. The guard duty ceremony is a Joseon-era military ceremony connecting the opening and closing of the city gates at Injeong and Paru with night patrol ceremonies, holding a position and role among the central military systems as important as guarding the royal palace.

The procedure for the 'Sungnyemun Gate Guard Duty Ceremony' begins with the guards lining up in front of their workplace at Sungnyemun Gate, followed by the appearance of the Geumru-gwan announcing Paru (bell tolling), and the signals of nagak (conch horn) and nabal (brass wind instrument). Under the command of the Hogun (military commander), the guards proceed with the Sungnyemun Gate opening ceremony. Afterwards, the guard duty ceremony to protect Sungnyemun begins, and the guard duty ceremony is performed after the duty shift between the 1st and 2nd guard units. Following six rounds of shift-changing and guard duty ceremonies, the guards proceed with the Sungnyemun Gate closing ceremony according to the Hogun's command.

spot_ev_4101384.title: 20th Century Photography Masters Exhibition - Light, Stopping Time
spot_ev_4101384.overview: In an era where hundreds of millions of images are easily born on liquid crystal screens and vanish lightly with a single tap of a finger. Amidst the flood of digital technology and artificial intelligence, anyone can easily capture and duplicate moments. Within the maze of light pixels, the heavy resonance and lingering imagery conveyed by analog photography are gradually fading. Amidst the repetition of easy production and consumption, we are losing the 'authenticity of gazing' at subjects deeply for a long time.
spot_ev_4101384.pull_quote: Seoul Jung-gu Recommended Seasonal Festival · Art Chosun Space (2026.11.20 ~ 2027.03.28)
paragraphs: In an era where hundreds of millions of images are easily born on liquid crystal screens and vanish lightly with a single tap of a finger. Amidst the flood of digital technology and artificial intelligence, anyone can easily capture and duplicate moments. Within the maze of light pixels, the heavy resonance and lingering imagery conveyed by analog photography are gradually fading. Amidst the repetition of easy production and consumption, we are losing the 'authenticity of gazing' at subjects deeply for a long time.

Since its inception, photography has been a physical exploration mediated by light and an art of time that captures and leaves behind a single cross-section of flowing time. The masterpieces born from the fingertips of 20th-century masters were not mere reproductions of phenomena through cold machines. They were the artists' unique philosophies that stared squarely at and interpreted the world. As a concept contrasting with digital images, analog-printed photographic works are called 'physical prints'. These are photographs completed as silver salt (photosensitive components combining silver and halogen elements) and platinum textures permeate the printing paper under the red light of a darkroom.

spot_at_1942237.title: Old Baekje Hospital, Busan
spot_at_1942237.overview: The Old Baekje Hospital is the first modern private general hospital building in Busan, serving as an important medical institution alongside Busan Municipal Hospital and Railway Hospital. According to the National Heritage Portal, the building was formed by combining two structures built in February and December 1927. After the hospital closed, it was used for various purposes, including a Chinese restaurant, Japanese military officer's quarters, Busan Police Headquarters, the Republic of China’s temporary embassy, and a wedding hall. After a fire in 1972, the fifth floor was demolished, and it currently stands as a four-story building.

spot_at_126028.title: Geumjeongsan Mountain
spot_at_126028.overview: Geumjeongsan National Geopark is a mountain formed by granite that solidified from magma underground about 70 million years ago, serving as the root of Busan's land. Visitors can admire the elegant granite formations shaped by years of wind and rain, including cliffs, tors, inselbergs, and block streams. The main peak, Godangbong, along with Janggunbong, Wonhyo-bong, and Sanghakbong, has fortresses built along the ridges connecting these peaks.
spot_at_126028.pull_quote: Local Recommended Partner · Nearby Restaurants & Safe Accommodation Routes
paragraphs: Geumjeongsan National Geopark is a mountain formed by granite that solidified from magma underground about 70 million years ago, serving as the root of Busan's land. Visitors can admire the elegant granite formations shaped by years of wind and rain, including cliffs, tors, inselbergs, and block streams. The main peak, Godangbong, along with Janggunbong, Wonhyo-bong, and Sanghakbong, has fortresses built along the ridges connecting these peaks.

These peaks and ridges feature unique tors, which are exposed remnants of large and small bedrock from the Cretaceous Bulguksa granite. The geology of Geumjeongsan consists of sedimentary rock layers from the Gyeongsang Group and volcanic rocks that intruded or erupted through them, along with the Bulguksa granite and Masan granite that intruded into these rocks. Registered as a national geopark, Geumjeongsan boasts beautiful scenery where bizarre rock formations and nature harmoniously coexist.

spot_at_975899.title: Old Dongchon Station, Daegu
spot_at_975899.overview: Located in Dong-gu, Old Dongchon Station began operations as a regular station in 1917 and was in service until 2008. It is the best-preserved station among the old Daegu Line stations and has retained much of its original 1930s architecture, earning it a designation as a registered cultural heritage site. The station features a wooden structure with a unique 'ㅅ'-shaped ceiling in the waiting room, and the design of the large gable of the waiting room and the small gable of the office is distinctive, allowing for clear visibility of the platform.
spot_at_975899.pull_quote: Local recommended partner · Nearby restaurants and safe accommodations
paragraphs: Located in Dong-gu, Old Dongchon Station began operations as a regular station in 1917 and was in service until 2008. It is the best-preserved station among the old Daegu Line stations and has retained much of its original 1930s architecture, earning it a designation as a registered cultural heritage site. The station features a wooden structure with a unique 'ㅅ'-shaped ceiling in the waiting room, and the design of the large gable of the waiting room and the small gable of the office is distinctive, allowing for clear visibility of the platform. Old Dongchon Station is architecturally significant due to its sharp gable roof design.

On May 15, 2008, the old Daegu Line was officially closed, and Old Dongchon Station was shut down along with Banya-wol Station. On April 1, 2014, Dongchon Park was established on the site of the old Daegu Line, and Old Dongchon Station was relocated and restored from Geomsa-dong in Dong-gu. Since May 17, 2014, it has been utilized as the 'Dongchon Station Small Library'. The park preserves part of the old railway tracks that were at Dongchon Station and has created an exhibition space within the Old Dongchon Station building.

spot_at_2746368.title: 2·28 Memorial Central Park
spot_at_2746368.overview: 2·28 Memorial Central Park was established to commemorate the 2·28 Student Democratic Movement. Opened in June 2003, it covers an area of 14,354㎡. The 2·28 Student Democratic Movement, which occurred in 1960, was a student-led protest in Daegu against the corrupt Rhee Syng-man regime, serving as a catalyst for the 3·15 Masan Incident and the 4·19 Revolution that ultimately led to the fall of the Rhee government. The park is located on the site of the former Daegu Central Elementary School, where traces of the 2·28 movement remain.

spot_at_128814.title: Ganghwa Samrangseong
spot_at_128814.overview: Samrangseong, located in Gilsang-myeon, Ganghwa-gun, Incheon, was a fortress built to defend Kaegyeong and Hanyang since the Goryeo Dynasty. The circumference is about 2.3 km, and the fortress follows the terrain of the mountain from the summit to the southern gate at an elevation of 75m, resulting in a significant height difference between the north and south. The three sons of Dangun were assigned to build each peak of Jeongjoksan, and people named this mountain fortress Samrangseong using the character for 'young man' (郞). It is also known as Jeongjoksanseong, located at an elevation of 222m south of Ganghwa Island.
spot_at_128814.pull_quote: Local Recommended Partners · Nearby Restaurants · Safe Accommodation Routes
paragraphs: Samrangseong, located in Gilsang-myeon, Ganghwa-gun, Incheon, was a fortress built to defend Kaegyeong and Hanyang since the Goryeo Dynasty. The circumference is about 2.3 km, and the fortress follows the terrain of the mountain from the summit to the southern gate at an elevation of 75m, resulting in a significant height difference between the north and south. The three sons of Dangun were assigned to build each peak of Jeongjoksan, and people named this mountain fortress Samrangseong using the character for 'young man' (郞). It is also known as Jeongjoksanseong, located at an elevation of 222m south of Ganghwa Island.

The exact date of construction is unclear, but it is estimated to have been built using rough natural talc, a technique from the Three Kingdoms period. In 1739 (15th year of King Yeongjo), the southern gate was rebuilt, and a gate tower was constructed, named Jonghaeru. It was again repaired in 1764 (40th year of King Yeongjo). In 1866 (3rd year of King Gojong), it was the site where Yang Heon-soo's troops defeated the French army. Inside Samrangseong is Jeondeungsa, the oldest temple in Korea and the largest temple in Ganghwa.

spot_at_1620578.title: Janggot Dondae
spot_at_1620578.overview: Janggot Dondae, located in Janghwa-ri, Hwado-myeon, Ganghwa-gun, Incheon, is a fortification from the late Joseon period. It was designated as an Incheon Metropolitan City monument on March 2, 1995. Along with Migot Dondae, Bukilgot Dondae, and Geomam Dondae, it is part of Janggot Fortress. Large-scale fortifications were constructed for coastal defense from the reign of King Hyojong to King Yeongjo, most of which were built in 1679 (5th year of King Sukjong). King Sukjong mobilized 8,000 soldiers from Hamgyeong, Hwanghae, and Gangwon provinces and 4,300 soldiers from the Royal Guard to build 49 fortifications in just 40 days.

spot_at_1953948.title: Gyo-dong Hyanggyo
spot_at_1953948.overview: Hyanggyo is an educational institution established by the state to honor the spirits of sages and conduct rituals, while also educating local citizens. Built in 1127 on the northern side of Hwacheong Mountain, it was relocated to its current site in 1741 and renovated in 1966. It is said that An Hyang brought a statue of Confucius from Yuan Dynasty on his way back from China in 1286, leading to the establishment of Confucian shrines in various towns in Seoul.

It is said that An Hyang brought a statue of Confucius from Yuan Dynasty on his way back from China in 1286, leading to the establishment of Confucian shrines in various towns in Seoul.

The remaining buildings include Myeongnyundang, which serves as an educational space, and Daeseongjeon, which is the ritual space, along with Dongmu and Seomu. Key attractions include Wolsunpo, where you can take photos with the Gyo-dong Bridge in the background, and various other sights.

spot_at_128823.title: Ganghwa Jangjeong-ri Stone Buddha Statue
spot_at_128823.overview: This stone Buddha statue from the Goryeo Dynasty is located beneath Bongcheonsan Mountain in Ganghwa County. Carved from thick granite slabs, it is now housed in a pavilion. Overall, it is grand and proportionate, though the large face, narrow shoulders, and big hands disrupt its balance somewhat. The statue stands 2.8 meters tall, with a prominent ushnisha on its head and a round face that carries a smile from the mouth to the cheeks and eyes. It reflects the characteristics of Goryeo-era statues.

spot_at_127575.title: Mudeungsan National Park (Gwangju)
spot_at_127575.overview: Mudeungsan was designated as a provincial park on May 22, 1972, and was designated as the 21st national park on March 4, 2013. Mudeungsan National Park covers an area of 75.425㎢ and is located in the northern and eastern districts of Gwangju, as well as in Damyang-gun and Hwasun-gun. The park is primarily composed of various types of rocks including Hwasun andesite, Mudeungsan tuff (quartz andesite tuff, Mudeungsan basalt, quartz andesite), Dogok volcanic rock, Mimu granite, biotite granite, quartz porphyry, and dike rocks.
spot_at_127575.pull_quote: Mudeungsan was designated as a provincial park on May 22, 1972, and was designated as the 21st national park on March 4, 2013. Mudeungsan National Park covers an area of 75.425㎢...
paragraphs: Mudeungsan was designated as a provincial park on May 22, 1972, and was designated as the 21st national park on March 4, 2013. Mudeungsan National Park covers an area of 75.425㎢ and is located in the northern and eastern districts of Gwangju, as well as in Damyang-gun and Hwasun-gun. The park is primarily composed of various types of rocks including Hwasun andesite, Mudeungsan tuff (quartz andesite tuff, Mudeungsan basalt, quartz andesite), Dogok volcanic rock, Mimu granite, biotite granite, quartz porphyry, and dike rocks.

The most notable feature of Mudeungsan is its columnar jointing. Columnar joints are formed when high-temperature lava cools on the surface, resulting in polygonal columns. These columnar joints can be well observed in the Mudeungsan columnar joint area (Seoseokdae, Ipsukdae, Gwangseokdae), Gyubong Rock, and Jungbong. Particularly, the highest peak of Mudeungsan, Cheonwangbong, at an elevation of 1,187m, features vertical jointed rocks that rise dramatically, resembling a stone wall. The rock formation known as Saeinbong, named for its resemblance to a jade seal, is located on the western ridge of Jangbuljae and consists of a curtain-like rock cliff.

spot_at_1330521.title: Chungjangno
spot_at_1330521.overview: If Myeongdong exists in Seoul, Chungjangno exists in Gwangju, Jeonnam. As the city expands, many new bustling streets have emerged, but the center of Gwangju will always be Chungjangno. Chungjangno was the main north-south road connecting the South and North Gates during the city wall era and was referred to as the city center. The commercial area on Chungjangno began to form shortly after the Japanese colonial period in 1911 when a Japanese national opened a general store called 'Yeomok' across from the current Industrial Bank.

paragraphs: If Myeongdong exists in Seoul, Chungjangno exists in Gwangju, Jeonnam. As the city expands, many new bustling streets have emerged, but the center of Gwangju will always be Chungjangno. Chungjangno was the main north-south road connecting the South and North Gates during the city wall era and was referred to as the city center.

The commercial area on Chungjangno began to form shortly after the Japanese colonial period in 1911 when a Japanese national opened a general store called 'Yeomok' across from the current Industrial Bank. After that, shops owned by Japanese nationals began to appear around Chungjangno 1-ga, and the reason they could dominate the commercial area was due to the presence of the Japanese Governor-General's office at the former provincial government site. The name 'Chungjangno' is derived from the posthumous title of Kim Deok-ryeong, a general during the Imjin War. The first streetlights on Chungjangno were oil lamps. Historically, it has been a hub for clothing, suits, and food services, attracting many young people and becoming known as a street of trends and youth.

spot_at_1621360.title: May 18th Democracy Square
spot_at_1621360.addr: 38 Munhwa Jeondang-ro, Dong-gu, Gwangju, South Jeolla Province
spot_at_1621360.overview: May 18th Democracy Square is located in front of the National Asian Culture Complex in Dong-gu, Gwangju. It commemorates the May 1980 Gwangju Uprising, which took place in front of the former Jeonnam Provincial Office. The square features a fountain, the Sangmu Hall, and a clock tower as symbols of the event, along with the Bell Tower of Democracy built in 2005, which rings on May 18th and Liberation Day.
spot_at_1621360.pull_quote: May 18th Democracy Square is located in front of the National Asian Culture Complex in Dong-gu, Gwangju.
paragraphs: May 18th Democracy Square is located in front of the National Asian Culture Complex in Dong-gu, Gwangju. It commemorates the May 1980 Gwangju Uprising, which took place in front of the former Jeonnam Provincial Office. The square features a fountain, the Sangmu Hall, and a clock tower as symbols of the event, along with the Bell Tower of Democracy built in 2005, which rings on May 18th and Liberation Day.

The old building that served as the Jeonnam Provincial Office was constructed in 1930 during the Japanese occupation and is now restored as the National Asian Culture Complex, designated as a national registered cultural heritage site since 1996. On May 14, 1980, students from Chonnam National University marched from the university to the square, joining forces with students from Chosun University and citizens to hold the National Democratic Grand Assembly, making it a symbolic site of the Gwangju Democratization Movement.

spot_at_126350.title: Wonhyo Temple (Gwangju)
spot_at_126350.addr: 1514-35 Mudeung-ro, Buk-gu, Gwangju, South Jeolla Province
spot_at_126350.overview: Wonhyo Temple is a traditional temple located in the majestic mountains of Mudeungsan, Gwangju, known for having the most beautiful pavilion in Korea. It is said that the temple was established by Wonhyo Daesa during the Silla period, who loved the beauty of the mountains. The name 'Wonhyoam' is derived from this history. Some say it was founded by a famous Huayan sect monk during the Goryeo period, who named it out of admiration for Wonhyo.

Some say it was founded by a famous Huayan sect monk during the Goryeo period, who named it out of admiration for Wonhyo. The subsequent history is hard to verify, but it is known that the temple regained prominence during the regency of Queen Munjeong, and it was also where the commander of the Joseon period, Yeonggyu, practiced. After being burned down during the Imjin War, it was reconstructed by Seokgyeong, who personally made the tiles for the restoration.

spot_at_127323.title: Gwangju Chung-hyo-dong Kiln Site
spot_at_127323.addr: 14 Pungamje-gil, Buk-gu, Gwangju, South Jeolla Province
spot_at_127323.overview: The kiln site located in Chung-hyo-dong, north of Mudeungsan, was used for producing celadon, buncheong, and white porcelain from the late Goryeo to the early Joseon period. The structure of the kiln includes access facilities, a firing room for placing pottery, and a chimney, resembling a connected round tomb shape. Based on records from the 'Annals of King Sejong' and the dating of excavated artifacts, it is believed to have started production around 1430.

spot_at_741957.overview: Daejeon Solomon Law Park is a legal education theme park operated by the Ministry of Justice. spot_at_945477.title: Uam Historical Park
spot_at_945477.overview: Uam Historical Park is an urban neighborhood park located in Dong-gu, Daejeon, where the great Confucian scholar Uam Song Si-yeol studied during the late Joseon Dynasty. From 1991 to 1997, buildings such as Jangpan-gak, a museum, and a Confucian academy were recreated, and it was reborn as a historical park on April 17, 1998. This park was established to honor and preserve the legacy of Uam Song Si-yeol, who flourished Confucian thought in this land during the late Joseon Dynasty. It contains historically significant cultural heritage, including Namganjeongsa, where Song Si-yeol taught his disciples in his later years, and Gikukjeong, known for its architectural beauty.

spot_at_3455349.title: 3.8 Democracy Movement Memorial Hall
spot_at_3455349.overview: The 3.8 Democracy Movement Memorial Hall is an exhibition and educational facility established to commemorate and inherit the history and spirit of the 3.8 Democracy Movement, which was initiated by high school students in Daejeon on March 8, 1960. This movement, a spontaneous democratization effort against the dictatorship and corruption of the Liberal Party regime, is recognized for its historical value as a national memorial day. The hall features permanent and special exhibitions showcasing historical materials, records, photos, and videos from that time.

spot_at_125994.title: Daejeon Expo Science Park
spot_at_125994.overview: Established to commemorate the 1993 Daejeon World Expo, which was the first international expo recognized by the Bureau International des Expositions (BIE) in Korea, this science park utilizes the facilities and grounds for public science education. The park features the Hanbit Tower, symbolizing a beam of light connecting the past, present, and future based on wise history. The 93-meter tall tower serves as an observatory inspired by science and space, offering views of the park and Daejeon city.

spot_at_126003.overview: The Honor Trail within the National Daejeon Cemetery is designed for veterans and visitors to walk comfortably while reflecting on the meaning of love for the country. spot_at_127542.title: Boramae Mountain Happiness Forest Trail
spot_at_127542.overview: The Boramae Mountain Happiness Forest Trail is a trail created around Boramae Mountain. Boramae Mountain (457.6m) was once called 'Treasure Mountain' because it was believed that treasures were buried there, and it is a beloved mountain in Daejeon. The trail circles around Boramae Mountain, returning to the starting point, and is approximately 13 km long. Visitors can walk comfortably in the shade of the dense trees, and in autumn, the foliage is impressive.

spot_at_3495467.title: Jangsaengpo Whale Culture District
spot_at_3495467.overview: The Jangsaengpo Whale Culture District is a cultural center for whales established in the Jangsaengpo area of Nam-gu, Ulsan. It is a historical area where whales have inhabited since prehistoric times, and it is the only tourist district in Korea where visitors can comprehensively experience the history and culture related to whales. The district is home to various exhibition and experience facilities focused on whale ecology and whaling culture. The main facility, the Jangsaengpo Whale Museum, displays various artifacts such as whale skeletons and whaling tools, while the Whale Ecology Experience Center is the first dolphin aquarium in Korea.

spot_at_125418.title: Sinbulsan Waterfall Natural Recreation Forest
spot_at_125418.overview: Sinbulsan Waterfall Natural Recreation Forest is located at the foot of Sinbulsan Mountain (1,159m), the second highest peak of the Yeongnam Alps, boasting beautiful mountain scenery over 1,000 meters above sea level. The surrounding valleys are filled with bizarre rock formations and diverse tree species, preserving the mysteries of ancient times. The clear and clean valleys provide abundant water, allowing visitors to experience both mental and physical healing. Unlike other recreation forests in the country, it is divided into upper and lower recreation areas, with the upper area known for its slow-paced environment.

A 30-minute walk leads to Pareuso Waterfall, known for its beautiful scenery.

spot_at_126091.title: Ilsan Beach (Ulsan)
spot_at_126091.overview: Adjacent to Daewangam Park, Ilsan Beach is an urban beach where you can enjoy stunning sea views during the day and beautiful nightscapes in the evening. Covering an area of 40,290㎡, with a length of 850m and a width of 42-61m, the beach has shallow waters and gentle slopes, making it perfect for family outings. The beach's Milky Way Plaza offers a resting area with soft lighting and a view of the sea, attracting many visitors year-round.

spot_at_126184.title: Seongnamsa Temple (Ulsan)
spot_at_126184.overview: Seongnamsa Temple is located at the eastern foot of Gajisan Mountain in Deokhyeon-ri, Sangbuk-myeon, Ulju-gun, and is a branch temple of Tongdosa, the main temple of the 15th district of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. The name Seongnamsa is derived from the fact that it is located south of Gajisan, which is also known as Seokmyeonsan. It is said that the monk Doi, who introduced Zen Buddhism to Korea during the reign of King Heondeok (the 41st king of Silla, 809-826 AD), discovered the site of Gajisan while searching for a sacred place.
spot_at_126184.pull_quote: Seongnamsa Temple is located at the eastern foot of Gajisan Mountain in Deokhyeon-ri, Sangbuk-myeon, Ulju-gun, and is a branch temple of Tongdosa, the main temple of the 15th district of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism.
paragraphs: Seongnamsa Temple is located at the eastern foot of Gajisan Mountain in Deokhyeon-ri, Sangbuk-myeon, Ulju-gun, and is a branch temple of Tongdosa, the main temple of the 15th district of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. The name Seongnamsa is derived from the fact that it is located south of Gajisan, which is also known as Seokmyeonsan.

The monk Doi, who introduced Zen Buddhism to Korea during the reign of King Heondeok (the 41st king of Silla, 809-826 AD), discovered the site of Gajisan while searching for a sacred place and established the temple to pray for the protection of Silla. After several reconstructions, the temple was destroyed during the Imjin War but was rebuilt in 1674 (the 15th year of King Hyeonjong) with the support of the local governor. Over the years, the temple fell into disrepair but was restored again in 1912 by Monk Uun, only to be devastated during the Korean War.
