spot_at_2675068.title: National Sejong Arboretum
spot_at_2675068.overview: The National Sejong Arboretum is the first urban national arboretum in South Korea. Adjacent to the Government Sejong Complex, it provides a space to experience nature within the city. Opened in October 2020, it is the second national arboretum following the National Baekdudaegan Arboretum, aimed at preserving and utilizing tree genetic resources by climate and vegetation types. The arboretum consists of three main areas: the Garden Exhibition Area, Plant Education Experience Area, and Community Participation Activity Area.
spot_at_2675068.pull_quote: The National Sejong Arboretum is the first urban national arboretum in South Korea. Adjacent to the Government Sejong Complex, it provides a space to experience nature within the city.
paragraphs: The National Sejong Arboretum is the first urban national arboretum in South Korea. Adjacent to the Government Sejong Complex, it provides a space to experience nature within the city. Opened in October 2020, it is the second national arboretum following the National Baekdudaegan Arboretum, aimed at preserving and utilizing tree genetic resources by climate and vegetation types. The arboretum consists of three main areas: the Garden Exhibition Area, Plant Education Experience Area, and Community Participation Activity Area.

The Garden Exhibition Area consists of nine gardens, including a traditional Korean garden that embodies the beauty of Korean tradition, a bonsai garden, a wildflower garden, a maple garden, an amphibian observation area, an ecological forest, a clear stream garden, an iris garden, and a wall garden. The Plant Education Experience Area has 11 spaces designed for understanding and experiencing plants, including a folk plant garden, a four-season exhibition garden, a rare and specialty plant garden, a forest garden, a garden plant measuring area, a forest restoration garden, a healing garden, a hibiscus garden, a children's forest experience area, a pollinator garden, and a commemorative garden for the IFLA World Landscape Architects Congress.
The Community Participation Activity Area is designed for citizen participation and leisure activities.

paragraphs: Hyoja Gang Yeong-cheon, a member of the Jinju Gang clan, lost his father at the age of three and lived with his widowed mother, Yeon-il Jeong. At the age of seven, his mother fell ill and became bedridden. Despite his young age, Yeong-cheon showed great filial piety. While caring for his sick mother, when her condition worsened and she lost consciousness, he broke his finger on the threshold to draw blood and let it flow into her mouth, collapsing.

His mother woke up to find her son bleeding and collapsed, and after careful nursing, he was able to wake up. The plaque hanging in front of the main gate reads, 'Hyoja Eobmugang Yeong-cheon Ji Mun-gak Gang Hee 39th Year Kyungjin March 15th Entry', indicating that this Hyoja Gate was built in the 26th year of King Sukjong (March 15, 1700). The original building was lost over nearly 290 years, and it was restored in 1987.

It is known as a place where kings visited from the late Goryeo to early Joseon periods to pray for the prosperity of the nation and the well-being of the people. At Mangyeongam, you can see the Mangyeongam Stone Buddha, designated as a Gyeonggi Cultural Heritage.

spot_at_128064.title: Gwanggyosan
spot_at_128064.overview: Gwanggyosan (582m above sea level) stretches about 2 km north and south between the Gyeongbu Expressway and the road connecting Seoul and Suwon, located in Sang Gwanggyo-dong, Suwon. spot_at_1955957.overview: Gueunsa Temple, located in Sagok 2-ri, Geunnam-myeon, Cheorwon-gun, is a shrine dedicated to the nine scholars who, in 1455 during the reign of King Danjong, retreated to the mountains due to their resentment over the usurpation of the throne by Suyang Daegun. These scholars (Kim Si-seup, Jo Sang-chi, Park Do, Park Jae, Park Gyu-son, Park Hyo-son, Park Cheon-son, Park In-son, Park Gye-son) dedicated their lives to the principles of integrity and loyalty.
spot_at_1955957.pull_quote: Gueunsa Temple, located in Sagok 2-ri, Geunnam-myeon, Cheorwon-gun, is a shrine dedicated to the nine scholars who...
paragraphs: Gueunsa Temple, located in Sagok 2-ri, Geunnam-myeon, Cheorwon-gun, is a shrine dedicated to the nine scholars who, in 1455 during the reign of King Danjong, retreated to the mountains due to their resentment over the usurpation of the throne by Suyang Daegun. These scholars (Kim Si-seup, Jo Sang-chi, Park Do, Park Jae, Park Gyu-son, Park Hyo-son, Park Cheon-son, Park In-son, Park Gye-son) dedicated their lives to the principles of integrity and loyalty.

The nine scholars lived in huts in the mountainous valleys of Geunnam-myeon, such as Yukdan-ri, Jamgok-ri, and Sagok-ri, focusing on agriculture while gathering to play Go and discuss worldly matters. However, as the times changed, they dispersed to various places. In the 9th year of King Injo's reign (1631), several scholars, including Lee Ji-yeon, gathered their intentions to build a shrine and held memorial ceremonies every spring and autumn. In 1865, during the Daewon-gun's order to abolish Confucian academies, the shrine faced destruction, but it was rebuilt in 1921 and restored again in 1977 with the help of local benefactors after being devastated during the Korean War.

spot_at_2569465.title: Yongam-ri Prehistoric Site
spot_at_2569465.addr: 1121 Yongam-ri, Hanam-myeon, Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon Special Self-Governing Province
spot_at_2569465.overview: The Yongam-ri prehistoric site in Hwacheon is a large-scale village site from the Bronze Age located in Hanam-myeon, Hwacheon-gun. This site is formed on the alluvial plain of the upper reaches of the Bukhan River, winding around the areas of Wirari and Yongam-ri. Excavations conducted by the Gangwon Historical and Cultural Research Institute from 2001 to 2003 revealed over 230 remains, including 176 house sites, 32 burial pits, 14 pillar-supported buildings, and 11 earthen tombs, showcasing the highest density of Bronze Age remains in the country.
spot_at_2569465.pull_quote: The Yongam-ri prehistoric site in Hwacheon is a large-scale village site from the Bronze Age located in Hanam-myeon, Hwacheon-gun.
paragraphs: The Yongam-ri prehistoric site in Hwacheon is a large-scale village site from the Bronze Age located in Hanam-myeon, Hwacheon-gun. This site is formed on the alluvial plain of the upper reaches of the Bukhan River, winding around the areas of Wirari and Yongam-ri. Excavations conducted by the Gangwon Historical and Cultural Research Institute from 2001 to 2003 revealed over 230 remains, including 176 house sites, 32 burial pits, 14 pillar-supported buildings, and 11 earthen tombs, showcasing the highest density of Bronze Age remains in the country.

The Bronze Age settlement formed in the Yongam-ri area is evaluated as a very important site that can shed light on the lifestyle and residential development of the Bronze Age in the Bukhan River basin, as well as the diffusion routes of Bronze Age culture, dating back to at least the 10th century BC to the 6th century BC. The site is also considered to have great preservation value as it is a rare village site in East Asia. A large quantity of stone tools, including chipped stone tools made from flakes, as well as various forms of stone axes and arrowheads, have been excavated. These stone tools exhibit complete or partially completed forms typical of Bronze Age remains.

spot_at_4139029.title: Woljeongsa Temple Stay
spot_at_4139029.overview: Woljeongsa is a thousand-year-old temple located on Odaesan Mountain, founded in 643 AD by the monk Jajangyulsa during the Silla Dynasty. The temple houses numerous national treasures, including an octagonal stone pagoda and a stone statue of a bodhisattva, and is famous for its beautiful path lined with over 1,700 towering fir trees. Woljeongsa offers year-round temple stays, providing an opportunity to experience the daily life of monks and learn about Korean Buddhist culture in a serene mountain setting. The temple stay program is divided into experiential and relaxation types.

Woljeongsa offers year-round temple stays, providing an opportunity to experience the daily life of monks and learn about Korean Buddhist culture in a serene mountain setting. The temple stay program is divided into experiential and relaxation types, with options available in English, Chinese, and Japanese.

The relaxation temple stay focuses on rest for two days and one night at the temple. Aside from meals, guests can enjoy free time walking along the fir tree path or meditating. The experiential temple stay involves participating in various programs over the weekend, focusing on rejuvenating the body and mind. Activities include meals at the temple, ceremonial prayers, making prayer beads, silent meditation, and tea time with monks. The prayer bead-making activity involves creating beads for each bow made during prayers.

spot_at_4096597.title: Hoengseong Catholic Church
spot_at_4096597.overview: This church showcases the modern church history of the Hoengseong area and the characteristics of post-war stone architecture. Originally, there was a chapel of Pungsuwon Catholic Church here, which was elevated to a parish in 1930, and a tiled wooden structure was built. After the original building was destroyed during the Korean War, the current stone church was constructed. The building features a Latin cross-shaped floor plan, and the interior mass space is designed as an auditorium without columns or walls.

The wooden truss above the main ceiling retains its original form from the time of construction. At the center of the front is an octagonal bell tower topped with a dome, housing a bell imported from France at the time of construction. Although the auxiliary buildings have changed several times, the exterior of the parish has mostly been preserved, showcasing the architectural style of the time. As a religious space where mass is still held, visitors should be mindful not to disturb the ceremonies and prayers of the congregation.

spot_at_2710737.title: Donghae Marine Resource Center
spot_at_2710737.overview: The Donghae Marine Resource Center, under the Korea Fisheries Resources Agency, works to preserve salmon, a key returning species along the East Coast, through breeding, nurturing, releasing, and creating natural spawning grounds. Over 70% of Korean salmon are born in the Namdaecheon River in Yangyang, where they grow for 3-4 years in the North Pacific before returning to spawn. However, due to river destruction, the number of returning salmon has decreased, prompting the center to perform artificial fertilization and hatch young salmon, which are then nurtured for about five months before being released into the Namdaecheon River.

Additionally, Mireuksaji, located below Haneuljae, is a significant temple site established during the early Goryeo period, flanked by Sinseonbong and Poamsan, with Wolaksan as the main mountain.

Poamsan features a unique combination of valley and ridge hiking. Most trails start from the Mireuksaji parking lot, passing through Haneuljae to the summit of Poamsan, leading to Mansubong and Yongambong. In Mansugol Valley, visitors can dip their feet in the stream, providing a refreshing break. The rocky paths are well-maintained, with wooden steps in some areas, though it can be crowded with hikers.

This path opens up to a refreshing breeze under the clear sky, surrounded by picturesque scenery of yellow pines, oak trees, and sea pines. Known as 'Haneuljae', the path leads down to a ditch that sometimes dries up due to drought, but is adorned with beautiful wildflowers like pink water lilies, deep purple swamp flowers, and yellow straw flowers. Although named Haneuljae (525m above sea level) as if it touches the sky, it is not particularly high.

Haneuljae serves as a boundary connecting Mireuk-ri in Chungju and Gwanum-ri in Mungyeong, taking about 30-40 minutes (2km) to walk from Mireuk-ri to Gwanum-ri. The rugged unpaved road leads to a smooth asphalt road at the top of Haneuljae, where the western peak of Daemisan (1,115m above sea level) comes into view. Additionally, the old temple site of Jungwon Mireuk-ri, believed to have been established during the late Silla to early Goryeo period, is located below Haneuljae.

paragraphs: Located below the village of Zhoune in Jangcheon-ri, Gagum-myeon, Chungju, Mokgye Solbat is an area of pine trees, historically known as Mokgye Naru. This area features 100-200 year-old pine trees and serves as a resting spot for vacationers during the summer. It is a 3,800-pyeong forest composed solely of pine trees, designated as a protected area by Chungju City. Mokgye Naru has a legend associated with it, one of which states that it became a significant inland waterway during the Joseon Dynasty.

However, Mokgye Naru suffered from major fires every year, causing significant damage. In search of a solution to these fires, a geomancer visited the area and suggested a method to redirect the waterway. The villagers transported soil from the river's center to create a mound, successfully redirecting the river towards Mokgye after more than six months, and planted many pine trees on that mound. This is how the Mokgye Solbat came to be.

Once known as Jijang-ri, this mountain basin village has a deep history, having been part of the Mahan territory during the Three Han period and a battleground during the Three Kingdoms era. The only existing Goguryeo stele, the Jungwon Goguryeo Stele, is located east of the village.

Sangdae Village is famous for its production of Cheongdo peaches and is home to many skilled artisans. Here, traditional crafts such as straw weaving, willow crafts, and wood crafts are preserved, along with traditional songs and liquors. Seasonal festivals like the Peach Blossom Festival in spring, the Starry Night Film Festival in summer, and the Mountain Music Concert in winter bring vitality to the village.

spot_at_917225.title: Seosan Haemi Eupseong Zelkova Tree
spot_at_917225.overview: In front of the southern Jin-nam gate of Haemi Eupseong, there is a large zelkova tree estimated to be around 300 years old. Locally, it is also called 'Hoya Tree'. In the late Joseon period, there was a prison behind the tree where persecuted Catholic believers were held, and between 1790 and 1880, those imprisoned were tortured by being hung from branches extending to the east of this tree. Recognized for its historical significance, it was designated as a cultural asset of Chungcheongnam-do in 2008.

spot_at_129184.title: Samgilpo Port
spot_at_129184.overview: Located at the northern tip of the Taean Peninsula, Samgilpo Port is the largest harbor among several along the Daehwa Embankment. It attracts many tourists from surrounding areas and the capital region. While the taste of sashimi prepared on the spot from fishing boats may be unmatched, the flavor of sashimi made from freshly caught fish offers a unique delight only found at the western sea ports. This area is particularly known for its abundance of black sea bream, which thrive in the brackish waters where seawater and freshwater meet.

There is also a memorial hall dedicated to those who participated in the Baekje Restoration Movement.

spot_at_125928.title: Birthplace of Lee Sang-jae
spot_at_125928.overview: This is the site of the birthplace of Lee Sang-jae (1850-1927), a social activist during the late Joseon Dynasty. Lee Sang-jae joined Christianity early on and worked to awaken the national spirit through faith movements. In the 18th year of Gojong's reign (1881), he visited Japan as a member of the Shin Sa Yu Ramdan and returned to serve as the secretary to the U.S. envoy Park Jeong-yang in the 25th year of Gojong's reign (1888). After returning from the U.S., he felt a strong need for new civilization and organized the Independence Association with Seo Jae-pil in the 2nd year of Gwangmu (1898) to lead the enlightenment of the people.

paragraphs: This is the site of the birthplace of Lee Sang-jae (1850-1927), a social activist during the late Joseon Dynasty. Lee Sang-jae joined Christianity early on and worked to awaken the national spirit through faith movements. In the 18th year of Gojong's reign (1881), he visited Japan as a member of the Shin Sa Yu Ramdan and returned to serve as the secretary to the U.S. envoy Park Jeong-yang in the 25th year of Gojong's reign (1888). After returning from the U.S., he felt a strong need for new civilization and organized the Independence Association with Seo Jae-pil in the 2nd year of Gwangmu (1898) to lead the enlightenment of the people.

In 1927, when the nationalist and socialist factions formed a united front to organize the New Korean Association with the goal of fighting against Japan, he was elected as the founding president. His works include the essay collections 'Young People' and 'The Foundation of the Nation for Young People'. The teacher's birthplace is a thatched house with an anchae (main house) and sarangchae (guest house), consisting of four rooms in the front and two on the side, with a gate featuring a raised design. The main house was built around 1800, and the guest house was constructed around 1926, but the original building was destroyed in 1955, and the current structure was restored in 1972 and 1980.

spot_at_129457.title: Shinseongni Reed Field
spot_at_129457.overview: Shinseongni Reed Field is a vast reed field formed at the confluence of the Geumgang River and the West Sea, recognized as one of the four major reed fields in Korea. It has been used as a filming location for various movies and dramas, including 'Joint Security Area (JSA)' and 'Kingdom', due to its beautiful scenery. The sunlight shimmering on the waves of the Geumgang River creates a mystical harmony, and in winter, it serves as a habitat for migratory birds such as swans and teal, making it a popular spot for nature study and photography.
spot_at_129457.pull_quote: Shinseongni Reed Field is a vast reed field formed at the confluence of the Geumgang River and the West Sea, recognized as one of the four major reed fields in Korea.
paragraphs: Shinseongni Reed Field is a vast reed field formed at the confluence of the Geumgang River and the West Sea, recognized as one of the four major reed fields in Korea. It has been used as a filming location for various movies and dramas, including 'Joint Security Area (JSA)' and 'Kingdom', due to its beautiful scenery. The sunlight shimmering on the waves of the Geumgang River creates a mystical harmony, and in winter, it serves as a habitat for migratory birds such as swans and teal, making it a popular spot for nature study and photography.

In particular, since the completion of the Geumgang River embankment in 1990, a large freshwater lake has been created nearby, attracting even more winter migratory birds. The reed field also showcases different colors and charms in each season, and it's delightful to experience the subtly different sounds of the reeds in the wind throughout the year. Observing the reed crab, which lives in the reed field, adds another layer of enjoyment. At the entrance, there is a reed experience center where you can learn more about reeds and the history and uses of the reed fields that were once much larger before agricultural land development.

spot_at_1608758.title: Maechang Park
spot_at_1608758.addr: 89 Maechang-ro, Buan-eup, Buan-gun, Jeonbuk Special Self-Governing Province
spot_at_1608758.overview: Maechang Park is a park created to commemorate the famous female writer Lee Mae-chang, who is known alongside Hwang Jin-yi and Heo Nan-seol-heon from the Joseon Dynasty. Lee Mae-chang (1573-1610) was a female poet during the reign of King Seonjo, known by the names Gyesaeng or Hyanggeum, with the courtesy name Cheonhyang and the pen name Mae-chang. Born as the daughter of Lee Tang-jong in Hyeon-ri, Buan, she excelled in poetry and was also skilled in music, particularly playing the geomungo (a traditional Korean string instrument).

paragraphs: Maechang Park is a park created to commemorate the famous female writer Lee Mae-chang, who is known alongside Hwang Jin-yi and Heo Nan-seol-heon from the Joseon Dynasty. Lee Mae-chang (1573-1610) was a female poet during the reign of King Seonjo, known by the names Gyesaeng or Hyanggeum, with the courtesy name Cheonhyang and the pen name Mae-chang. Born as the daughter of Lee Tang-jong in Hyeon-ri, Buan, she excelled in poetry and was also skilled in music, particularly playing the geomungo.

Buan County has created a cultural park featuring a stone monument inscribed with Lee Mae-chang's poetry, along with a forest, Mae-chang Theme Exhibition Hall, Wetland Park, Buan Cultural Center, and Yu Hee-gyeong Plaza. Additionally, there are facilities for children, walking paths, and basketball courts. The park is adorned with trees and flowers, and sculptures and resting areas have been installed throughout the walking paths. At night, the park is illuminated, allowing for a charming evening stroll. The Buan Masil Festival is held in May at Maechang Park.

spot_at_128977.title: Jinan Hyanggyo
spot_at_128977.addr: 13-6 Hyanggyo-gil, Jinan-eup, Jinan-gun, Jeonbuk Special Self-Governing Province
spot_at_128977.overview: Jinan Hyanggyo was established in 1414 (the 14th year of King Taejong) to enshrine the spirits of virtuous scholars and to educate and enlighten local residents. It was destroyed during the Imjin War and rebuilt in 1601 (the 34th year of King Seonjo), and relocated to its current site in 1636 (the 14th year of King Injo). The existing buildings include the Daeseongjeon, Myeongnyundang, Beonandan, and Seojae, where the spirits of five sages, four Confucian scholars from the Song Dynasty, and eighteen scholars from Korea are enshrined.
spot_at_128977.pull_quote: Jinan Hyanggyo was established in 1414 (the 14th year of King Taejong) to enshrine the spirits of virtuous scholars and to educate and enlighten local residents.
paragraphs: Jinan Hyanggyo was established in 1414 (the 14th year of King Taejong) to enshrine the spirits of virtuous scholars and to educate and enlighten local residents. It was destroyed during the Imjin War and rebuilt in 1601 (the 34th year of King Seonjo), and relocated to its current site in 1636 (the 14th year of King Injo). The existing buildings include the Daeseongjeon, Myeongnyundang, Beonandan, and Seojae, where the spirits of five sages, four Confucian scholars from the Song Dynasty, and eighteen scholars from Korea are enshrined.

The Daeseongjeon is a place where the spirits of Confucian scholars, including Confucius, are honored. It has a scale of three bays in the front and two bays on the side, with a gable roof that resembles the character '人' when viewed from the side. Rituals are held in spring and autumn, and during the first and fifteenth days of the month, incense is offered. The collection includes 95 types of printed books and 11 types of manuscripts, totaling 106 types and 198 volumes.

spot_at_128973.title: Jinan Eunsusa Cheongsil Pear Tree
spot_at_128973.addr: Dongchon-ri, Maryeong-myeon, Jinan-gun, Jeonbuk Special Self-Governing Province
spot_at_128973.overview: The Cheongsil pear tree is a species similar to the sandol pear tree, growing near homes or in the mountains. The leaves are oval-shaped with serrated edges, and both sides are hairless and firm. The fruit is brown or green and ripens to yellow in the fall. The Cheongsil pear tree growing in the Eunsusa Temple in Jinan is estimated to be over 640 years old. The tree has a unique appearance, with a large trunk splitting into four branches at the top, supporting the upper part.
spot_at_128973.pull_quote: The Cheongsil pear tree is a species similar to the sandol pear tree, growing near homes or in the mountains.
paragraphs: The Cheongsil pear tree is a species similar to the sandol pear tree, growing near homes or in the mountains. The leaves are oval-shaped with serrated edges, and both sides are hairless and firm. The fruit is brown or green and ripens to yellow in the fall. The Cheongsil pear tree growing in the Eunsusa Temple in Jinan is estimated to be over 640 years old.

The tree has a unique appearance, with a large trunk splitting into four branches at the top, supporting the upper part. This area is influenced by the terrain, and when the wind blows, the firm leaves of the Cheongsil pear tree shake and create an indescribable sound. Additionally, in winter, if water is placed next to the base of the Cheongsil pear tree, icicles can form upside down towards the tips of the branches. The Cheongsil pear tree is a native Korean species, and there are not many left today, making large trees especially rare and designated as a natural monument. The Eunsusa Cheongsil pear tree is currently surrounded by a fence, with an information sign installed nearby.

Deogyusan spans across Jeollabuk-do Muju and Jangsu, as well as Gyeongsangnam-do Geochang and Hamyang, with its highest peak, Hyangjeokbong, reaching 1,614 meters.

spot_at_126958.title: Heuksuksan Natural Recreation Forest
spot_at_126958.addr: 306 Sangol-gil, Gyegok-myeon, Haenam-gun, Jeonnam Gwangju Unified Special City
spot_at_126958.overview: Heuksuksan Natural Recreation Forest is located on Heuksuksan Mountain (650m above sea level), the sacred mountain of Gyegok-myeon. The name 'Heuksuk' was recorded as 'Choeum' in the Daedongyeojido, a map of Korea created during the Joseon Dynasty by the cartographer Kim Jeong-ho. Originally called Gahaksan, the name 'Gahak' was given because the mountain resembles a crane soaring. 'Heuksuk' derives from the black appearance of the mountain's rocks after rain. In spring, beautiful azalea fields and the best cluster of sosan trees in Korea can be found here.

The children's forest experience center conducts forest experience activities for kindergarteners, and the foot bath experience center allows visitors to soak their feet and relax in the refreshing forest air. paragraphs: The living quarters and garden of Haechang Brewery were built in 1927 by Shibada Hikobei, who was born in Gunma Prefecture, Japan, and settled in Haenam after passing through Gangjin. After liberation, the eldest son, Moon, who founded Samhwa Elementary School in Haenam, lived here, and the brewing license is believed to have been issued by him in 1961. Subsequently, Hwang Uigwon, who was engaged in the brewing industry, took over Haechang Brewery and brewed alcohol for over 30 years. Since 2008, the couple Oh Byeong-in and Park Ri-a have been operating the brewery.

Haechang Brewery, filled with over 40 species of trees, began to gain recognition for its beautiful garden. It was featured in KBS in 2011, KBS in 2012, and the Chosun Ilbo in 2013, leading to an increase in visitors from afar. In 2014, it was designated as a 'visiting brewery' by the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs due to its beautiful garden and the presence of modern cultural heritage nearby. The name 'makgeolli' is believed to have two meanings: one referring to 'freshly filtered alcohol' and the other to 'lightly filtered alcohol.' The Haechang makgeolli brewed here is known for its non-sweet taste and craftsmanship.

spot_at_128807.title: Gocheonamho (Migratory Bird Habitat)
spot_at_128807.addr: Gocheonam-ro, Hwangsan-myeon, Haenam-gun, Gwangju Metropolitan City
spot_at_128807.overview: Gocheonamho is the largest reed habitat in South Korea. The Gocheonam reed fields host rare birds such as the black stork and eagles, as well as 90% of the world's migratory swans that perform spectacular dances during winter. A total of 54 bird species (excluding unidentified species) have been observed, making it the largest migratory bird habitat in the country, with 33 species of waterfowl, 5 species of raptors, and 16 other bird species.

spot_at_231919.title: Haenam Myeongnyang Battle Monument
spot_at_231919.addr: 34 Usuyoungan-gil, Munnam-myeon, Haenam-gun, Gwangju Metropolitan City
spot_at_231919.overview: The Haenam Myeongnyang Battle Monument was erected to honor Admiral Yi Sun-sin for his victory in the Battle of Myeongnyang in 1597. The inscription was written in 1686, and the monument was erected by Park Sin-joo, the naval commander of Jeolla Province, in 1688. The monument features a rectangular base with a body and a headstone adorned with clouds and dragons. The inscription records Admiral Yi's efforts to regroup his navy after the Battle of Chilcheollyang and his victory over the Japanese forces using the swift currents between Usuyoung and Jindo.

spot_at_1624224.title: Kim Nam-joo's Birthplace
spot_at_1624224.addr: 98 Bonghak-gil, Samsan-myeon, Haenam-gun, Gwangju Metropolitan City
spot_at_1624224.overview: Kim Nam-joo is a representative figure of Korean national literature, known as a 'warrior poet' who passionately advocated for social change and a 'national poet' who awakened the Korean literary world with his revolutionary voice. He was also a revolutionary poet who spent a decade in prison fighting against dictatorship. Born in 1945 in Bonghak-ri, Haenam-gun, Gwangju Metropolitan City, he attended Samhwa Elementary School and Haenam Middle School before enrolling in Gwangju Ilgo, but he dropped out in opposition to exam-oriented education.
spot_at_1624224.pull_quote: Kim Nam-joo is a representative figure of Korean national literature, known as a 'warrior poet' who passionately advocated for social change and a 'national poet' who awakened the Korean literary world with his revolutionary voice. He was also…
paragraphs: Kim Nam-joo is a representative figure of Korean national literature, known as a 'warrior poet' who passionately advocated for social change and a 'national poet' who awakened the Korean literary world with his revolutionary voice. He was also a revolutionary poet who spent a decade in prison fighting against dictatorship. Born in 1945 in Bonghak-ri, Haenam-gun, Gwangju Metropolitan City, he attended Samhwa Elementary School and Haenam Middle School before enrolling in Gwangju Ilgo, but he dropped out in opposition to exam-oriented education.

During his time in university, he participated in the 'Three-Term Constitutional Amendment Opposition Movement' and produced the first underground newspapers 'Hamsung' and 'Gobal' in the country during the anti-Yushin movement, which led to an 8-month prison sentence and his expulsion from university. In 1974, he debuted in the literary world with works like 'Jinhonga' in 'Creation and Criticism' and later formed the 'People's Culture Research Institute' with writers like Hwang Sok-yong. In 1978, he was active as a 'warrior' in the strongest underground organization against Yushin, 'Namminjeon', until he was arrested with his comrades in October the following year.

spot_at_126637.title: Osan (Gurye)
spot_at_126637.addr: 303 Saseongam-gil, Muncheok-myeon, Gurye-gun, Gwangju Metropolitan City
spot_at_126637.overview: Osan is recorded in the Bongseongji as 'the shape of the rock is outstanding, resembling Geumgangsan, and has been called 'Little Geumgang' since ancient times.' It is a 531m high mountain facing Jirisan, known for its gentle slopes and beautiful scenery, making it a popular destination for family outings and group picnics. Saseongam is a temple built on the sheer cliffs of Osan, established by the monk Yeongi in the 22nd year of King Seong of Baekje (544 AD), originally called Osanam, and later renamed Saseongam after four great monks (Uisang, Wonhyo, Doseon, and Jinjakguksa) meditated here.

paragraphs: Osan is recorded in the Bongseongji as 'the shape of the rock is outstanding, resembling Geumgangsan, and has been called 'Little Geumgang' since ancient times.' Saseongam is a temple built on the sheer cliffs of Osan, established by the monk Yeongi in the 22nd year of King Seong of Baekje (544 AD), originally called Osanam, and later renamed Saseongam after four great monks (Uisang, Wonhyo, Doseon, and Jinjakguksa) meditated here.

spot_at_126767.title: Dangmol Spring
spot_at_126767.addr: 3-2 Jangsu-gil, Masang-myeon, Gurye-gun, Gwangju Metropolitan City
spot_at_126767.overview: Sangsa Village is recognized as one of the longest-living villages in the country, along with Yangcheon Village in Ganjeon-myeon, Gurye-gun. The locals attribute their longevity to the clean environment of the Simsan Valley and 'Dangmol Spring'. Dangmol Spring is renowned for its exceptional health benefits, with locals claiming that 'the water from the roots of medicinal herbs in Jirisan flows here.' In 1986, a water quality test by a preventive medicine team from Korea University found it to be the best water in the country, with no E. coli detected. According to the local Kim clan, their ancestor discovered Dangmol Spring while searching for a good location in Jeolla Province during the late Joseon period.

King Munmu, who unified the Three Kingdoms, requested that his body be cremated in a Buddhist manner and that his ashes be buried in the East Sea to prevent invasions by Japanese pirates. This rock is known as Daewangam or Daewang Rock, and the underwater royal tomb is unique in the world. Daewangam was created using natural rocks, with artificial waterways shaped in a cross pattern in the rock island, and a small pond was dug in the center to form a harbor.

paragraphs: This mural tomb, excavated in January 1985 by the Cultural Heritage Administration and Daegu University, is designated as a historic site and is a valuable resource both academically and culturally. The construction date of this tomb is estimated to be around 539 AD based on the inscription 'Gimi Jungmyo Sanginmyeong' found on the southern wall of the tomb's chamber. The internal structure is a stone chamber tomb with an entrance, leading to the chamber where the body is enshrined.

The chamber measures approximately 3.5m east-west and 2m north-south, with walls that slightly taper towards the top, and the ceiling is completed with two large flat stones. The murals cover all walls and the sides of the chamber, except for the ceiling, with particularly strong warrior figures painted on the left and right walls of the entrance. Notably, the warrior figure on the west wall, holding a snake, is interpreted as a guardian of this tomb.

spot_at_2029190.overview: Musoe Dal Village, located in Punggi-eup, Yeongju, is the starting point of the Sobaeksan 3 Jarak-gil and is traversed by the old Juknyeong road. The name 'Musoe Dal' means 'Iron Bridge.' Long ago, there was an iron bridge in this village, which is how the village got its name. Although it is now called Sucheol-ri Musoe Dal Village, the old name of Sucheol-ri was also Sucheolgyo (水鐵橋) ri. The symbolic iron bridge of the village is no longer preserved in its original form, but you can find a sculpture that recreates its appearance in Musoe Dal Village.

spot_at_250281.title: Gyeongju Inwang-dong Temple Site
spot_at_250281.overview: The Inwang-dong Temple Site in Gyeongju is believed to be the former location of Inyongsa Temple. Mentioned in the 'Samguk Yusa' (Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms), Inyongsa was built to pray for the well-being of Kim In-mun (629–694), the second son of King Muyeol of Silla. According to historical records, after Goguryeo fell, Tang China attempted to conquer Silla and imprisoned Kim In-mun, who was staying in Tang. The people of Silla opened a Avalokitesvara ritual to pray for his return, but when Kim In-mun died in 694 (the 3rd year of King Hyoso's reign) on his way back home, the ritual was converted into an Amitabha sanctuary to pray for his rebirth in the Pure Land. Inyongsa is the first recorded temple in Silla built for a private individual rather than a monk or royal family member, reflecting the religious practices of the time. Excavations were conducted four times between 2002 and 2011 by the National Research Institute of Cultural Heritage. It features a typical Silla twin-pagoda temple layout, alongside a rare '亞' (A-shaped) building site, pagoda sites, a main hall site, lecture hall site, corridor site, lotus pond, and a well.

paragraphs: The Gyeongju Inwang-dong Temple Site in Gyeongju is believed to be the site of Inyongsa Temple. Featured in the 'Samguk Yusa', Inyongsa was a temple built to pray for the well-being of Kim In-mun (629–694), the second son of King Muyeol. According to records, after the fall of Goguryeo, Tang China attempted to conquer Silla and imprisoned Kim In-mun, who was staying in Tang.

The people of Silla held a Gwaneum (Avalokitesvara) ritual praying for his return, but when Kim In-mun died in 694 (the 3rd year of King Hyoso's reign) while returning home, they changed it to a Mita (Amitabha) ritual to pray for his peaceful afterlife. Inyongsa is the first temple in Silla built for a private individual rather than a monk or a monarch, showing the form of faith at the time. Excavations were carried out in four phases from 2002 to 2011 by the National Gyeongju Research Institute of Cultural Heritage. Featuring a typical Silla twin-pagoda layout, a rare '亞'-shaped building site, pagoda sites, main hall site, lecture hall site, corridor site, lotus pond, and well have been identified.

spot_at_2599775.title: Sangju Heossi Silk Fabric
spot_at_2599775.overview: Heossi Silk is carrying on the 5th generation of traditional silk weaving from silkworm cocoons, one of the key specialties of Sangju, a region famously known for its 'three whites' (rice, silk, and dried persimmons). spot_fo_2838772.overview: Milmyeon (wheat noodles) is a dish created by North Korean refugees who evacuated to Busan during the Korean War. The Gyeongju Milmyeon Main Branch inherited this noodle-making technique to faithfully recreate the authentic taste of traditional milmyeon. The noodles are freshly kneaded and pulled upon ordering, served in a broth simmered for 24 hours with Korean beef bones, medicinal herbs, and various vegetables. paragraphs: Motjae is a pond located on the summit of Jisan Mountain to the west of Naecheon-ri, Yulgok-myeon, Hapcheon-gun. While some say it is a crater lake formed by a volcanic explosion, it is presumed to have been created by natural subsidence. A plant called watershield (sunchae) grows naturally here. In the past, this plant was considered a miraculous remedy for leprosy, skin diseases, and jaundice, prompting many patients to visit in search of medicinal herbs to cure their illnesses. It is also said that nearby residents used to gather on the surrounding lawn to divide into teams and build camaraderie through folk wrestling (ssireum) matches.

Additionally, during the Imjin War, Japanese troops camped here and engaged in battle with our righteous army stationed at Baengmasanseong Fortress opposite. The surrounding Jisan Park, located just north of Cheonjimot Pond, is a community amenity featuring an octagonal pavilion, lawns, and shady trees where local residents enjoy picnics. Cheonjibong Peak, at the summit of Cheonjimot, offers breathtaking panoramic views in all directions, and on the first full moon of the lunar new year, residents burn large moon-welcoming fires (daljip) to pray for a bountiful harvest and peace. Known as Dalmaji-bong (Moon-gazing Peak), it is a naturally occurring resort deeply rooted in history and scenic beauty.

spot_at_2611161.title: Oepo Port, Geoje
spot_at_2611161.overview: Designated as a national fishing port in December 1971 and currently managed by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Oepo Port spans 0.8 km in width with an inner harbor depth of 8m and outer harbor depth of 22m. As the nation's premier Pacific cod distribution center—accounting for over 30% of the country's cod supply—the port comes alive every day at 10 AM with the booming voices of auctioneers at the Oepo-ri fish market. Packed with fresh cod, it is a wonderful place to enjoy invigorating cod soup.

spot_at_128947.title: Hwangsan Village Traditional Stone-Mud Walls, Geochang
spot_at_128947.overview: The ancient stone-mud walls of Hwangsan Village in Geochang enclose traditional houses belonging to the Geochang Sin clan lineage. The village preserves houses built from the late Joseon Dynasty to the modern era, offering a glimpse of a traditional Korean settlement. Large natural stones are stacked at the base without mortar to ensure good drainage, topped with alternating layers of small stones and clay. Most walls are capped with traditional Korean tile roofing (hansik giwa). The gently curving walls harmonize with historic houses to create a serene landscape.

spot_at_127042.title: Mireukdo Island, Tongyeong
spot_at_127042.overview: Mireukdo is an island south of Tongyeong connected to the mainland by two bridges and an undersea tunnel. Its highlight is the Sanyang Coastal Circular Road, famous for offering the ultimate Hallyudo marine scenery with beautiful coastal curves, hills, and quiet fishing ports. Donam-dong, the starting point of the circular road, features marina resorts and cruise terminals heading to nearby Hansando, Bijindo, Maemuldo, and Geoje Haegeumgang. Further south, Dala Park features benches and pavilions for viewing breathtaking sunsets over the southern sea. Yonghwasan Mountain in the center houses Yonghwasa and Miraesa temples, and walking the quiet forest trail between them is a must-do experience.
spot_at_127042.pull_quote: Mireukdo is an island south of Tongyeong connected to the mainland via bridges and an undersea tunnel. Its coastal circular road offers gorgeous sea curves...
paragraphs: Mireukdo is an island south of Tongyeong connected to the mainland by two bridges and an undersea tunnel. Mireukdo's coastal highlight, the Sanyang Circular Road, is famous for offering breathtaking views of the Hallyu archipelago, featuring stunning coastline curves, hills, and tranquil harbor scenery.

Donam-dong, the starting point, features marina resorts for water sports and cruise terminals offering trips to nearby Hansando, Bijindo, Maemuldo, and Geoje Haegeumgang, along with lodging and amenities. Dala Park on the south side of the road offers benches, resting areas, and a pavilion to enjoy dazzling sunset views over the South Sea. Meanwhile, Yonghwasan Mountain in the center features Yonghwasa Temple to the north and Miraesa Temple to the south; walking the tranquil hiking trail connecting both temples is a true highlight of Mireukdo tourism.

spot_at_126660.overview: Mireukdo is an island within Hallyeohaesang National Park, serving as a hub for South Sea marine tourism and connected to the mainland via Chungmugyo Bridge. Designated as a special tourist zone, it offers diverse leisure opportunities. A major landmark is Mireuksan Mountain, rising in the center of the island. Visitors can take the Hallyudo Viewing Cable Car completed in 2008 to the summit for panoramic views of the archipelago. Though not exceptionally tall, Mireuksan is celebrated for its lush forests and clear streams, showcasing royal azaleas in spring and brilliant foliage in autumn.

Well-maintained hiking trails allow for a light two-hour hike. A popular course starts from Yonghwasa Square, passes Gwaneamsa Temple and Mireukjae to reach the summit, and descends via Miraesa Temple and Ttibat back to Yonghwasa Square. Living up to its reputation, marine tourism is highly developed here, offering yachting, cruises, windsurfing, kayaking, and water skiing. Cruise ferries connecting to Hansando, Bijindo, and Maemuldo in Tongyeong's coastal waters are popular leisure activities for all ages. Additionally, the Musical Fountain Rest Plaza offers sweet melodies and colorful laser shows.

Their signature menus are grilled beotgul and steamed beotgul, and they also sell beotgul pancakes, seasoned freshwater clam salad, and freshwater clam soup. Their homemade plum makgeolli (rice wine), made by adding homemade plum extract to makgeolli brought from a nearby brewery, pairs wonderfully with the food. Beotgul are shucked right next to you before serving, making them easy to eat. Grilling them in a charcoal kiln with their shells on and pairing them with red chili paste (chogochujang) or aged kimchi delivers an exceptional taste.

paragraphs: This is one of the walking trail courses where you can enjoy works of art imbued with the breath of artists alongside Jeju's beautiful ocean scenery. Located where Jeju's freshwater and seawater meet, the observatory offers views of Seopseom Island straight ahead, Seogwipo Port to the right, and Munseom Island. It is said that the painter Lee Jung-seop spent his happiest times catching crabs with his wife and two sons on the Jaguri coast, where Seopseom and Munseom Islands are visible.

spot_at_591798.title: Hagosudong Beach
spot_at_591798.overview: Located in the sea northeast of Seongsanpo at the eastern tip of Jeju Island, Hagosudong Beach on the volcanic island of Udo is divided into two sections by a rocky coastline exposed in the center. The total length of the beach is about 400m, with basalt reefs exposed around 100m and 200m–300m to the east, and dune layers developed in the background. The beach was formed by the accumulation of materials transported by coastal currents. Until the 1970s, anchovy fishing using traditional 'huritgeum' (haul nets) took place here.

spot_at_591866.overview: Located in Hallim-eup, Jeju-si, Geumneung Beach is directly connected to Hyeopjae Beach, a popular spot on the western coast. While it shares a similar landscape with its neighboring beach—featuring a sea that looks like dissolved blue paint, the cute-shaped Biyangdo Island, and soft sandy shores—its charm lies in being less crowded and more leisurely. The parking lot connects directly to the beach, making it hassle-free to carry your belongings. The newly built shower facility is equipped with hot water showers for added convenience...

paragraphs: Located in Hallim-eup, Jeju-si, Geumneung Beach is directly connected to Hyeopjae Beach, a popular spot on the western coast. While it shares a similar landscape with its neighboring beach—featuring a sea that looks like dissolved blue paint, the cute-shaped Biyangdo Island, and soft sandy shores—its charm lies in being less crowded and more leisurely. The parking lot connects directly to the beach, making it hassle-free to carry your belongings. The newly built shower facility is equipped with hot water showers for added convenience. When visiting this place, we recommend timing your visit to match the low tide.

When the seawater recedes far out, a wide, fine sandy beach is revealed. Natural pools with shallow depths, perfect for young children to play in, are formed in various spots. Seaweed and small sea snails left behind by the receding seawater naturally become toys for the children. Thanks to this, you can have a fun time even if you visit without any special preparation. However, since crushed seashell fragments are mixed with the sand at the beach entrance, wearing water shoes is strongly recommended. (Source: Visit Jeju Website)

Walking through scenes of old downtown areas, moon villages, retro dance halls, tea rooms, and comic book shops modeled after traditional marketplaces, older generations can reminisce while younger generations who haven't experienced those times can imagine the lives their parents once lived.

spot_at_601489.title: Seogwipo Marine Provincial Park
spot_at_601489.overview: This is a marine provincial park centered around the coast of Seogwipo-si, Jeju Special Self-Governing Province. Recognized as one of the 75 scenic views of Seogwipo, it is well-known as the quintessential Seogwipo coastal scenic spot, featuring coastal cliffs spanning about seventyri east and west around Seogwipo City harmonizing with islands floating on blue waves. Boasting beautiful scenery, it is the southern limit habitat for globally rare distylium trees (machilus thunbergii) and the natural monument black pigeon.
spot_at_601489.pull_quote: This is a marine provincial park centered around the coast of Seogwipo-si, Jeju Special Self-Governing Province. Recognized as one of the 75 scenic views of Seogwipo, it is well-known...
paragraphs: This is a marine provincial park centered around the coast of Seogwipo-si, Jeju Special Self-Governing Province. Recognized as one of the 75 scenic views of Seogwipo, it is well-known as the quintessential Seogwipo coastal scenic spot, featuring coastal cliffs spanning about seventyri east and west around Seogwipo City harmonizing with islands floating on blue waves. Boasting beautiful scenery, it is the southern limit habitat for globally rare distylium trees and the natural monument black pigeon.

It also represents the biodiversity of southern marine species as a site featuring prominent geological columnar joints and numerous new or unrecorded species of Korean endemic marine life with high academic value. To maintain ecological order through marine ecosystem resource conservation and create new tourism trends by maximizing resource utilization, Seogwipo Marine City Park was converted into Seogwipo Marine Provincial Park in January 2007. It is particularly well-known as a wonderful spot for sunrises and sunsets. Furthermore, located at the entrance of Cheonjeyeon Waterfall, the park serves as a relaxing station for those returning after fully absorbing the beauty of the waterfall.

spot_at_635928.title: Choinamdan Tangerine Experience Farm
spot_at_635928.overview: Choinamdan Tangerine Experience Farm is a citrus harvesting farm located in Namwon-eup, the southernmost part of Seogwipo-si. spot_at_660972.title: Hado-ri Migratory Bird Habitat
spot_at_660972.overview: Located in Hado-ri, Gujwa-eup, Jeju-si, this migratory bird habitat is adjacent to the sea and boasts abundant nutrient-rich prey and wetland plants, making it an optimal region for migratory birds to spend the winter. Designated as a natural monument, the area welcomes about 30 species of migratory birds every year, including the black-faced spoonbill—of which only about 1,600 remain worldwide—as well as natural monuments like swans, falcons, and kestrels, and the Ministry of Environment's endangered wild animal, the osprey.

spot_at_2452856.title: Seoul Guui Water Purification Plant Plant 1 & 2 (Former Guui Arisu Water Purification Center)
spot_at_2452856.overview: The Guui Arisu Water Purification Center is a place where you can see the history of South Korea's water purification facilities at a glance. Plant 1, built in 1936, and Plant 2, built in 1959, produced tap water until 2002 and were registered as National Registered Cultural Heritage in 2007. Here, visitors can explore an exhibition hall that details Seoul's tap water, Arisu, and take a tour of the water treatment process. Additionally, the Guui Arisu Cultural Heritage Tour Program is operated, offering customized content tailored to different age groups such as children, teenagers, and adults. Children aged 6-7 learn about the water environment experienced at the purification plant where Han River water becomes tap water, while teenage student groups explore topics such as when tap water was first created and where the Arisu in school drinking fountains comes from. For adults, the program features a tour of the historic Guui Plant 1 and Plant 2. The program runs twice a day on weekdays, at 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM, and applications can be made through the Seoul Public Service Reservation website or by phone.

spot_at_3483083.title: Gansong's Former House (Gansong Yeotjip)
spot_at_3483083.overview: Gansong's Former House is a traditional hanok with a history of about 100 years that retains the traces of Gansong, who made a great contribution to safeguarding Korea's cultural heritage, and is harmoniously situated alongside the gravesite of Gansong Jeon Hyeong-pil (1906–1962). The old house was built in the late 19th century by his adoptive father Jeon Myeong-gi (1870–1919) for the purpose of managing a nearby farm and crop yields coming from northern Gyeonggi Province and Hwanghae-do. Following his father's death, a gravesite was established near the hanok, and it was also used as a ritual pavilion (jaesil) to store ritual implements needed for memorial services and ancestral rites, and to hold ancestral rites on the daecheongmaru (wooden floor) of the main hanok in case of bad weather. Gansong frequently visited and lived here when visiting the farm in Yangju-gun or holding memorial services for his father. During the Korean War, the main gate, part of the wall, and the buildings suffered damage. After the war, repairs were delayed due to the restoration of damages to his main home in Jongno-gu and Bohwagak. Following Gansong's passing in 1962 and the demolition of his Jongno main home, partial repairs were made using salvaged materials.

spot_at_2599899.title: Daegu Dongseongno Street
spot_at_2599899.overview: Dongseongno literally means the road created by tearing down the eastern fortress wall of Daegu Eupseong (Daegu Town Fortress). Spanning from the Dongseongno 28 Art Square to CGV Daegu Hanil and Daegu Station sections, it is Daegu's representative commercial center. Dongseongno encompasses Banwoldang Station and Dalgubeol-daero to the south, and Jungang-daero or the Jongno area to the west (extending north to Daegu Station and east to Gongpyeong-ro). Famous as a Daegu landmark overflowing with youth and romance, Dongseongno is fully equipped with numerous fashion brand stores where you can catch the latest trends, as well as exhibitions, performances, and food options. The area is so well-organized that even first-time visitors can easily navigate without getting lost. Because you can find various clothing brands in one place, many young people actually prefer shopping here over department stores. The fact that the stores are large-scale adds to the fun of shopping.

spot_at_128627.title: E-World
spot_at_128627.overview: Located in Dalseo-gu, Daegu, E-World is a downtown-style theme park that has established itself as one of Daegu's representative tourist attractions since its opening in 1995. Centered around Daegu's iconic landmark, the 83 Tower, the park offers a wide array of attractions, seasonal festivals, performances, and events for endless entertainment from day to night. Featuring everything from heart-pounding thrill rides to family-friendly content suitable for visitors of all ages, it also includes a petting zoo called Zoo Farm, as well as various dining and convenience facilities. In spring, the park blooms with cherry blossoms and tulips; summer brings water play and night views; autumn showcases cosmos and themed festivals; and winter lights up with a sledding slope, Christmas events, and nightscapes. From the 83 Tower, visitors can enjoy panoramic views of downtown Daegu. Combining sightseeing and leisure all in one place, E-World is loved by families, couples, and friends alike.

spot_at_250329.title: Daegu Christian History Museum (Daegu Jeil Church)
spot_at_250329.overview: Established in 1893, Daegu Jeil Church is the oldest church in Daegu and Gyeongsangbuk-do province. It stands in the heart of the Yakryeongsi Herbal Medicine Street, alongside the Yakryeongsi Museum of Oriental Medicine and the Daegu Gyenam YMCA Building. It faces Gyesan Catholic Cathedral, Daegu's first Catholic cathedral, across Seoseong-ro Street. Historically, because it was located within the fortress walls, it was also called Seongnae Church, and having been situated inside the southern gate, it was referred to as Nammunan Chapel or Nammunnae Church. The building features a classic Gothic style, evoking an exotic West European atmosphere. It stands two stories tall with a 33-meter-high, five-story bell tower. Due to its location, it serves as a major tourist hub during the Yakryeongsi Hanbang Culture Festival and other major Daegu festivals, and is included in Daegu city tours and modern alley walking courses. The original chapel was established in 1896 by purchasing a traditional Korean hanok house (initially named Namseongjeong Church), before a second chapel was built in 1908. This second chapel was a single-story structure built collaboratively by American missionaries and traditional Korean carpenters, featuring a central bell tower that doubled as the entrance, flanked by symmetrically arranged vertical windows. Its tin roof, windows, and bell tower were considered remarkably exotic and wondrous by the citizens of Daegu at the time, remaining a popular sight for many years. Demolished in 1931, a new two-story third chapel was completed in 1933, and the name was changed to Jeil Church. In 1936, a Gothic bell tower was added, creating its current appearance. The bell tower features uniquely designed windows from the first to fifth floors, topped with an octagonal spire. Due to its architectural and historical significance, the main sanctuary and bell tower were designated as Daegu Tangible Cultural Heritage No. 30 in 1992. The building is a simple Gothic structure with a rectangular floor plan oriented north-south, featuring an entrance at the center of the front facade and a bell tower on the right. Boasting the longest history among Daegu's numerous church buildings, Daegu Jeil Church serves as a valuable asset for researching modern architectural history as a symbol of Christianity's contribution to modernization. Although a new main sanctuary was built in Doksan-dong in 1994, this site functioned as Daegu Jeil Church for over a century. Today, it operates as a Christian History Museum right next to the Yakryeongsi Museum of Oriental Medicine. The museum exhibits various artifacts used during the enlightenment period, including Bibles, hymnals, and offering boxes, alongside historical photographs. It also records and displays the history, timeline, and missionary activities of Daegu Jeil Church. As a church that participated in the March 1st Independence Movement of 1919, it also features an interactive space where visitors can make rubbings of the Declaration of Independence.

spot_at_1115613.title: Suseongmot Lake Amusement Park
spot_at_1115613.overview: Suseong Amusement Park is located at the lower foot of the ridge extending northwest from Yongjibong Peak (629m) in Beommul-dong, creating a scenic natural landscape blending gentle surrounding mountains with Suseongmot Lake. Created in 1925, the lake boasts a water capacity of 700,000 tons, a surface area of 218,000㎡, and a perimeter of 2,020 meters. Originally constructed as an artificial reservoir for agricultural irrigation during the Japanese colonial period in 1925, Suseongmot Lake now serves as a waterfront relaxation space, boasting abundant water levels year-round. The surrounding area features benches, trees, walking paths, a cruise ship dock, and Suseong Land, an amusement park equipped with rides such as spaceships, cruise boats, viking ships, bumper cars, and merry-go-rounds. Offering sights and activities like boat rides, duck pedal boats, a children's playground, and Dusan Waterfall, it is the ideal spot for family outings and romantic dates. The Suseongmot Media Art Music Fountain offers a unique visual spectacle. ◎ Travel Info to Experience Hallyu's Charm - Suseongmot Amusement Park, where the drama characters Robin and Hana prepared for a sad farewell, is a representative healing spot for Daegu residents. At night, visitors can enjoy lighting around the pond, downtown nightscapes, and dazzling fountain shows.

spot_at_1116203.title: Unamji Waterside Park
spot_at_1116203.overview: Unamji Waterside Park is a nature-friendly park created around Unamji Reservoir at the foot of Hamjisan Mountain. Designated as the 3rd of the 8 Scenic Views of Buk-gu, Daegu, it is a beloved spot for citizens to enjoy both water and lush woodlands. Unamji Reservoir is known to have been established around the Japanese colonial period in a valley surrounded by rolling hills 200 to 300 meters above sea level, including Hamjisan Mountain, serving as a reservoir supplying agricultural water to the nearby Chilgok fields. This waterside park was developed by preserving the reservoir in its natural state after large-scale housing development in the Chilgok District 3 of Daegu, harmonizing seamlessly with the surrounding environment.

spot_at_2672393.title: Haeundae Blue Line Park
spot_at_2672393.overview: Haeundae Blue Line Park is a key tourist facility in Haeundae Special Tourist Zone, Busan—an international tourist city—created by eco-friendly redeveloping the old 4.8km railway facility of the Donghae Nambu Line spanning from Mipo to Cheongsapo and Songjeong in Haeundae. Operating along gorgeous coastal scenery, it features the Haeundae Beach Train and Haeundae Sky Capsule. The Haeundae Beach Train is a tourist train combined with public transit that runs round-trip from Haeundae Mipo through Cheongsapo to Songjeong, allowing passengers to admire the stunning coastal views of eastern Busan. The Haeundae Sky Capsule is a romantic 4-seater automatic capsule that travels a 2km section from Mipo to Cheongsapo on an aerial rail 7 to 10 meters high, offering mystical coastal views.

spot_at_2733472.title: Hwangnyeongsan Mountain Observatory
spot_at_2733472.overview: Hwangnyeongsan Mountain, home to the Hwangnyeongsan Observatory, spans across four districts of Busan (Busanjin-gu, Yeonje-gu, Suyeong-gu, and Nam-gu), making it a mountain located right in the center of the city. In spring, the roads draped with blossoming cherry blossoms on both sides are popular driving courses. It also boasts optimal conditions as a night view destination well-known even to outsiders, thanks to the path leading up to the observatory. The colorful glowing transmission towers and cozy lights illuminating the observatory make the panoramic view of Busan sprawling beneath the mountain look even more breathtaking. Visitors can enjoy coffee and meals while admiring the scenery using the indoor and outdoor facilities. The first basement level is designed to allow groups of around 60 people to host special events.

In addition, it is equipped with optimal conditions as a night view spot known even to out-of-towners, as the road leads straight up to the Hwangnyeongsan Observatory. The first basement level is designed so that about 60 group customers can host special events.

spot_fo_2616370.title: Geumjeongsanseong Changnyeongjip
spot_fo_2616370.overview: This restaurant has been selling duck and black goat dishes since 1980, starting with boiled chicken (baeksuk) made from home-raised chickens upon the requests of students and picnickers looking for snacks to accompany Sanseong Makgeolli. Taking immense pride in black goat dishes—a local culinary specialty of Busan—they continuously research and develop traditional black goat bulgogi recipes. They use domestic black goats and ducks, and serve vegetables harvested directly from their own garden. In addition, they have independently developed a matured seasoning infused with medicinal herbs to set themselves apart. Offering a free jokgu (foot volleyball) court for outdoor leisure activities, it is an ideal spot for group gatherings or dinners, and is popular for allowing visitors to rest in the fresh air while enjoying a meal.

They use domestically sourced black goats and ducks, and provide vegetables grown in their own garden. They also stand out by using a self-developed aged sauce infused with herbal medicines. spot_at_1957694.title: Yongdusan Jagalchi Tourist Zone
spot_at_1957694.overview: The Yongdusan Jagalchi Tourist Zone is an attractive cultural tourism area brimming with history and culture. It is a representative old-downtown tourist destination where you can feel the pulse of history through storytelling locations such as Bosudong Book Street, 40-Step Culture and Tourism Theme Street, and International Market (Gukje Market), alongside delicious street foods like fish cakes, seed hotteok (sweet pancakes), bibim dangmyeon (mixed glass noodles), red bean porridge, and patbingsu (shaved ice). The tourist zone is packed with rich historical and cultural resources of the old city center, including the Yongdusan Park Observatory with views of Namhang Port and Yeongdo, Gwangbok-dong shopping district, Jagalchi Market filled with seafood and eateries, Gukje Market for diverse shopping, Bupyeong Kkangtong Night Market for local foods and shopping, Yeongdo Bridge, Bosudong Book Street, and the Busan Modern History Museum. As an urban tourist destination enabling year-round events, festivals, and shopping, it is a thriving spot frequented by domestic and international tourists alike. The restoration of Yeongdo Bridge's bascule lift offers a differentiated spectacle unseen elsewhere, emerging as a new tourist landmark. Coupled with the endless transformation of traditional markets—such as the opening of global complex cultural spaces at Bupyeong Kkangtong Night Market and Gukje Market—alongside events like the Busan International Film Festival, Busan Jagalchi Festival, and Busan Christmas Tree Festival, this tourist zone is full of new sights and entertainment.

spot_at_1960620.title: Busan Jagalchi Yanggopchang Alley
spot_at_1960620.overview: If you exit through Exit 10 of Jagalchi Station on the Busan Subway, you will find Jagalchi Yanggopchang (Beef Tripe and Intestines) Alley right in front. Named for its location near Jagalchi Market, this area has long been thriving with gopchang restaurants and is a popular spot for intestine lovers. Interestingly, many restaurants here feature a unique layout where multiple vendors operate inside a single large shop, requiring visitors to choose a specific stall upon entering, alongside traditional standalone restaurants. Operating hours vary by restaurant, so it is recommended to check in advance. The restaurants have maintained the traditional method of grilling yanggopchang over briquette fire, offering a mix of specific cuts in salt-grilled (sogeum-gui), seasoned-grilled (yangnyeom-gui), and hot pot (jeongol) varieties.

spot_at_2605602.title: Oeyangpo Artillery Battery
spot_at_2605602.overview: Oeyangpo is a port located at the southern tip of Gadeokdo Island in Gangseo-gu, Busan. In February 1904, the Japanese military, having sparked the Russo-Japanese War, designated Oeyangpo as a military base to secure a stronghold around the Korea Strait, forcibly evicting 64 households. Afterward, to build a naval base, the Japanese dispatched the 3rd Temporary Fortification Unit to complete construction and deployed the 2nd Company of the Jinhae Bay Fortress Artillery Battalion. Soon relocating the artillery battalion headquarters to reinforce troops, Oeyangpo became a military base prepared for naval battles against the Russian fleet. The village of Oeyangpo still retains numerous Japanese-style buildings presumed to be military facilities—such as battery headquarters, official residences, offices, barracks, and warehouses—which continue to be used as residences by local residents.

spot_at_2946224.title: Gwangju Chungjang-ro K-Pop Star Street
spot_at_2946224.addr: 94 Chungjang-ro, Dong-gu, Jeonnam Gwangju Metropolitan City (Chungjang-ro 2-ga)
spot_at_2946224.overview: K-Pop Star Street was created to improve the aged surrounding scenery and commemorate K-pop stars originally from Jeonnam Gwangju Metropolitan City who practiced singing and dancing there since their obscurity days. The street is brightly illuminated with lighting and pole signs, broadcasting K-pop videos and fan videos via electronic billboards and wall media facades. It features murals depicting singers' album jackets, benches decorated with song titles, handprints, and sculptures. After BTS member J-Hope personally visited and posted a verification shot on a colorful bench themed around a BTS song, the street became a sanctuary for fans. Leaving behind his impressions and a message of gratitude, it is an essential course that no 'ARMY' should miss.

spot_at_3006671.title: Neoritjae Old Road
spot_at_3006671.addr: 1 Nammun-ro, Dong-gu, Jeonnam Gwangju Metropolitan City (Seongyo-dong)
spot_at_3006671.overview: Neoritjae Old Road is an old mountain pass stretching about 4.3 km between Seongyo-dong in Dong-gu, Jeonnam Gwangju Metropolitan City, and Hwasun-eup, serving since ancient times as a major transportation route connecting Gwangju and the southeastern region. Imbued with historical significance alongside the natural scenery of Mt. Mudeungsan's foothills, it bears traces of modern and contemporary Korean history, including the Donghak Peasant Revolution and the Korean War. Known to originate from the names 'Neoljae' or 'Neol-ui Jae', it remained an old path after the opening of the Neoritjae Tunnel in 1971. Today, it has been developed into a pleasant walking forest trail where visitors can enjoy lush forests and changing seasonal scenery. Especially in spring, cherry blossoms bloom in full along the pass, offering a breathtaking view.

spot_at_1621388.title: Gwangju Jisan-dong Five-Story Stone Pagoda
spot_at_1621388.addr: Jisan-dong, Dong-gu, Jeonnam Gwangju Metropolitan City
spot_at_1621388.overview: Located to the east of the two pagodas standing at a considerable distance apart within downtown Jeonnam Gwangju Metropolitan City, this is a stone pagoda from the late Unified Silla period. The area where the pagoda stands is known to be the site of Baegjusa Temple, though no conclusive evidence has been discovered yet. During its disassembly and repair in 1955, sarira (Buddhist relics) reliquary was discovered on the upper surface of the 4th-story roof stone, and it was repaired again in 1961 with some stone materials reinforced. Among the few remaining five-story stone pagodas in the region, it is an outstanding example from the late Unified Silla period. Pagodas are structures enshrining Buddha's cremated remains, and even if actual remains are absent, they are considered to symbolically enshrine them. The Jisan-dong Five-Story Stone Pagoda of Jeonnam Gwangju Metropolitan City was previously called the 'Gwangju East Five-Story Stone Pagoda' because it stood on the eastern side of Gwangju. Built with a five-story body (stupa body) atop a two-tiered foundation (stylobate), it is topped with a decorative head (mast top). The foundation serving as the pagoda's base consists of multiple stones, while both the body and roof stones are each carved from a single piece of stone. Notably, only the first-story roof stone support has five tiers, while the second story and above each have four tiers, indicating that it follows the late Unified Silla architectural style.

Notably, only the first-story roof stone support has five tiers, while the second story and above each have four tiers, indicating that it follows the late Unified Silla architectural style.

spot_at_1623995.title: Birthplace of Danjae Shin Chae-ho
spot_at_1623995.overview: The Birthplace of Danjae Shin Chae-ho is where the independence activist and historian Danjae Shin Chae-ho was born and spent his childhood until the age of 8. Born as the second son of Shin Kwang-sik in Dorimi Village, he moved to Cheongju, Chungcheongbuk-do, after losing his father at a young age. He entered Sungkyunkwan at 19 and became a Sungkyunkwan scholar (doctor) at 26. Following the Eulsa Treaty in 1905, he engaged in media activities to inspire national consciousness and led the enlightenment movement against Japanese colonial rule. Later, involved in the Sinminhoe (New People's Association) anti-Japanese secret society case, he went into exile in Vladivostok in 1910 to carry out independence activities. He was eventually arrested by the Japanese police in 1928, imprisoned in Lushun Prison, and died in prison on February 21, 1936, at the age of 57. In the summer of 1992, his birthplace was excavated, surveyed, and restored to a thatched-roof house based on local historical research, along with the installation of a bronze statue of Shin Chae-ho. It was designated as a Daejeon Metropolitan City Monument on July 10, 1991.

spot_at_1907645.title: Invention Education Center Creative Invention Experience Center
spot_at_1907645.overview: The Creative Invention Experience Center at the Invention Education Center is located inside the International Intellectual Property Training Institute in Yuseong-gu, Daejeon. Opened in December 2005, the center spans a total floor area of 1,200 pyeong across one basement level and three floors above ground, featuring facilities such as creative invention experience rooms, exhibition halls, and lecture rooms. It provides diverse invention education opportunities to talented young innovators selected from various regions. Utilizing experienced professionals from the Daedeok Research Development Special Zone, Korean Intellectual Property Office examiners, and school invention teachers as instructors, the center offers advanced invention education along with practical hands-on programs that foster students' creativity and challenging spirit. To help students easily understand and experience invention through play and fun, the center is organized into four thematic zones: 'Click, Imagination Icon', 'Seeing the Power of Imagination', 'Bearing the Fruit of Imagination', and 'Imagination Becomes Reality'.

spot_at_2765276.title: Gyodongdo Ferry Terminal Waiting Room (Wolsunpo)
spot_at_2765276.overview: This is the waiting room located at the Gyodongdo Ferry Terminal (Wolsunpo) in Ganghwa. In the past, before the opening of the Gyodong Bridge, the ferry terminal was the area's only gateway, but since the bridge opened in 2014, it now carries the quiet charm of a small port. Although the waiting room itself is closed, the building remains intact, evoking nostalgic memories. To let visitors enjoy the close-up sea views, rocking chairs, benches, and charming photo zones have been installed around the port, making it an increasingly popular spot for visitors, as well as a favorite destination for fishing and car-camping.

spot_at_129283.title: Jumundo Island
spot_at_129283.overview: Jumundo is one of the four islands located in Seodo-myeon, Ganghwa-gun, Incheon, renowned alongside Boleumdo as a scenic island. According to legend, during the late Joseon Dynasty, General Im Gyeong-eop submitted a farewell letter to the king in Hanyang from this island while traveling to China as an envoy. Originally called Jumundo (奏文島, meaning the island where a memorial was presented), its hanja characters later changed to the current Jumundo (注文島). During the reign of King Injo of the Joseon Dynasty, it belonged to the Gyodong Naval Command, holding strategic and geographical importance as evidenced by the dispatch of a naval commander and the operation of a state-run ranch. Major tourist attractions on the island include Daebinchang, Apjangsul, and Dwijangsul beaches, as well as Bonggusan Mountain situated in the center. In particular, rugosa rose (haedanghwa) colonies form around Daebinchang and Dwijangsul beaches, offering breathtaking scenery during the summer months.

spot_at_1620526.title: Hueaedondae Watchtower
spot_at_1620526.overview: A 'dondae' is a type of historical military outpost built in strategic border or coastal areas with high visibility to monitor enemy movements and prepare for attacks. Featuring high outer fortress walls and lower inner areas, they were designed to house cannons. As one of Ganghwa's 53 dondae watchtowers, Hueaedondae was constructed in a square shape using granite and features four platforms for cannons, maintaining relatively well-preserved conditions. Portions of the low wall built atop the fortress remain uniquely intact, leading to its complete restoration in 1998. Local legends say that damaging this watchtower brings disaster, which prompted villagers to protect it like an altar, preserving its original appearance to this day. Built in 1679 (the 5th year of King Sukjong's reign), the construction mobilized 2,000 royal guards and 8,000 monk soldiers from Gyeonggi, Chungcheong, and Jeolla provinces. (Source: Korea Heritage Service)

spot_at_128819.title: Ganghwa Anglican Church
spot_at_128819.overview: Consecrated in 1900 by Bishop Mark Trollope (known as Goyohan in Korean), Ganghwa Anglican Church was originally named Saints Peter and Paul Church. The construction was led by chief royal palace carpenters, and while it has undergone a few repairs since then, its original appearance remains well-preserved. The church site was shaped like a boat to symbolize the ark of salvation for the world. The church building features a rectangular (4 bays wide, 10 bays long), multi-layered structure that follows traditional Korean architectural styles, while its layout and interior apply Western basilica architecture, showcasing a harmonious blend of beauty and indigenous spirit. Initially designated as a Gyeonggi-do Tangible Cultural Heritage in 1981, it became an Incheon Tangible Cultural Heritage when Ganghwa-gun was incorporated into Incheon, and was re-designated as a Historic Site in January 2001.

spot_at_1857095.title: Kim Sat-gat-myeon, Yeongwol [Slow City]
spot_at_1857095.overview: Yeongwol-gun is a harmonious blend of mountains, water, and valleys. Beyond its stunning natural scenery, visitors can retrace the footsteps of King Danjong—the tragic king who lost his throne at a young age and was put to death—and Kim Sat-gat, the wandering and genius poet of the late Joseon Dynasty. Well-preserved pristine natural environments such as Gossi-gul Cave (a Natural Monument) and Kim Sat-gat Historic Site make it an optimal destination for experiencing tranquility and relaxation. To commemorate Kim Sat-gat's era spirit of humor and satire, as well as his artistic soul, cultural festivals are held every October to re-illuminate his literary value. Backed by such rich cultural resources and recognized for its preservation value, it has been designated as an International Cittaslow (Slow City). Moreover, Yeongwol-gun is designated as a Special Museum District, with as many as eight museums located solely in Kim Sat-gat-myeon, its core content area. Through the museum cultivation project, the region attracts museums reflecting local characteristics, strengthens competitiveness, and discovers invisible value through talent cultivation, network building, themed experience programs, and cultural product development. Various museums are operated here, including Byeolmaru Observatory, Nango Kim Sat-gat Literature Museum, Yeongwol Y Park, Danjong History Museum, Donggang Museum of Photography, Yeongwol Cave Ecology Museum, Gangwon-do Coal Mine Literature Village, Donggang Ecology Information Center, Yeongwol Radio Star Museum, and Art Creation Studio.
